I bought the game a long time ago, when it was more or less dead. However now there's been a recent surge of players, meaning that there'll be more than two servers populated at a time. I'd recommend to buy this game now while there's still players around as it is a genuinly unique and fun experience.
The game is an RTS/FPS hyprid. One team will take the role of spacemarines and one of an Alien race.
Spacemariens have a selection of weapons and gadgets in the form of assaultrifles and shotguns to grenadelaunchers, flamethrowers and mechs. Can instead morph into different types of creatures, each with a unique role to fullfill.
One player on each team will take the role of a commander who will order structures to be built, special AI units to be ordered in aswell as researching new creatures/weapons. This person will play from an RTS perspective. It's very important that all players on a team follows the commanders commands; building resourcegatherers, powernodes and deffensive structures, aswell as coordinating assaults on enemybases.
Gameplaywise this game is great. Fans of oldschool shooters will be delighted by the fast-paced, twitchy, first-person combat. Both factions have their unique little quirks which causes an interesting dynamic that helps each game feel unique. Marines will need to capture and fortify powernodes and build their bases around them, fortifying with mines and sentryguns. After the proper research has been done, footsoldiers will unlock jetpacks, grenades and exosuits which help elevating the gameplay to new and interesting heights. Aliens will however need to take a more stealthy aproach to combat, setting up ambushes by climbing up above doors, dropping down on marine footsoldiers aswell as traversing in the cover of ventelationshafts, before unlocking stronger alien creatures with wings, fast leaps, as well as the large rhino-esque brute: Onos, which can wreck havoc upon enemy structures. Aliens can only build through a slime-cushion which needs to be spread by the commander, with assistance from the players.
For the time, the game is graphically gorgeus, albeit poorly optimized. Walking into a pitch-dark room knowing that an alien creature have just recently busted a powerbox with only your flashlight giving you some sanctuary in the hostile dark is an uniqely atmospheric multiplayer experience that only this game has done so far. Crawling through vents in order to safely get out of a marines shootingrange, climbing across walls and soaring through the air are all satisfying gameplay aspects of the game which helps to really put yourself into the shoes of the creatures you play as. This game is proof that a twitchy, competetivly viable game can still be atmospheric.
Communitywise... it's a mixed bag. When I originally bought the game, when it had just more or less died, every player still around was an impatient, toxic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Experienced players would join the one populated rookie-server, proceed to stomp the life out of them and/or votekick every rookie on the server, effectivily conquring it. Even though new players were trying hard to communicate with the commander, asking for advice and following their waypoints, they would be kicked as soon as possible. I've never understood this mentality in dying games. When new players are obviously trying to get into the game, why would you completly freeze them out like this ON THE ROOKIE SEVRERS? Nowadays I would consider the situation much, much better. People seem overall more tolerant and friendly nowadays and you'll generally find a handfull of beginnerservers filled with people who are either willing to learn, or ready to learn out. Even stil, you'll every now and then encounter your typical unhelpfull elitist ruining everyone's fun.
I genuinely hope that this game will be brought back to life as it is one of the most fun,, balanced, varied and unique multplayer experiences I've ever played. The developers seem like an active bunch with pasion for their game. Hopefully I've been able to convince you to purchase this game and help us build a stable playerbase. At only 10€ it's a steal. This is the kind of game I'd love to see an active modding community behind it, with an active esports scene to spread it's popularity. I can't say anything else than that this might be one of the best multiplayer game available on the PC and therefor it deserves to be treated as such!

10,000,000 is a match 3 puzzle game dressed up with RPG elements. The tiles you match correspond to your characters actions as he travels the games "dungeon", i.e. match keys to unlock doors. There are also stone and wood tiles which allow you to upgrade your home base, which allows you to upgrade your character between runs; and a couple of different attacks to help with monsters. It's very subject to the whims of the RNG so some runs can end very quickly whilst others will have everything fall into place with little effort. Pun not intended. The graphics are a little rough around the edges but do their job and the same could be said of the audio, all in all this is a cheap time waster that is sometimes fun, sometimes frustrating. I  wouldn’t want to pay more than $2 for it but it has its charm and a nice RPG gimmick to separate it from other match 3's.
- Lots of gameplay
- Fun, when you get on a good run
- Graphics are simple and unpolished. They do the job, but thats about all they do
- A little too luck dependent for me
- Grindy
Recommended only if you are a huge fan of this type of game

Bloons TD battles has 82% positive reviews (3k+). I decided this is the guarantee that game is good. So I installed it.
First of all, this is mobile port. Big buttons, mobile UI, etc..I don't like mobiles port, but this subjective opinion doesn't make game bad.

You start a game, place some towers and send green baloons. Next wave starts, you send red baloons and place some towers. Next wave starts you send blue baloons and place some towers... Repeat these actions until your enemies leaks 50 (random colour) baloons or you became totally bored to continue play this game too.
Yeah, pvp mechanic in TD games is pretty innovative. But I don't understand how people like play each battle the same way. There is no information how much health each baloon has. There are no types of armor/damage. There are no tower characteristics. So there is totally no tactics in the game. Just send "new colour" baloons. It's not a tower defense game because TD game is a strategy game. Bloons TD Battles isn't a strategy game. It's just a casual game for people who like do thoughtless and repetitive actions.
I would recommend to play Kingdom Rush third time instead of playing this horrible game.

When i saw this game on sale as always i looked at the community page and the first post i saw was "Why haven't you already bought this game?" Funny if it was directly speaking to me but alas it wasn't though it was just that post that persuaded me to buy the game with no idea to what i had just bought.
And it was one of the best things i have done. I could say this game is just amazing and end it at that but that would not give the game credit. Like a machine can only work while all parts are oiled this game combines all of its elments together to form one of the best games i have ever bought.
The game blends some platforming elements, puzzels, exploration and hack and slash fighting together without making any element unwanted or overused. All rely on the other to work and produce a fun gaming experience.
The games graphics are of a high quality with each area you visit varying so that no two areas are the same. The monsters are a bit samey but they vary enough with new monsters in each area. When Dust talks to npcs you can tell that the person producing the art put a lot of effort into their job.
The combat controls are very fluid. Admittedly you could win the game just by mashing buttons but if you take time to learn the combos it vastly improves the gameplay. There are also some enemies where normal attacks deal little or in some cases no damage prompting you to learn different ways to defeat enemies else in one area you find yourself hopelessly surrounded. Combat also evolves as the game progresses with certain enemies gaining new skills that test your abilities the way games should test new skills. One personal problem i had with the button layout was that the health button was next to the attack button so i would be spawning health instead of attacks but that could have been rectified if I had changed the the keyboard layout.
The character animations look good with battles looking very artful, each moveset looks stunding as you progress in your use of combo moves and again the artstyle is breathtaking.
Added into the game is a crafting system that does seem a bit gimmicky as enemies drop items without the need to collect items and pay money though the game improves on the grinding element by almost completely removing it. Once you get an item you can sell it to a merchant and they will begin to stockpile the goods for you. Something i see as very welcome.
But all of this pales in comparison to the story. I would admit the plot would seem quite easy to work out, with many hints comming from characters and that i all i will give away. Trust me the story is the best part of the game. Along with the story many of the characters have their own distinct personalities, a point i find lacking in many games. The games progression and developing of characters creates some who you will just come to love more and more.
The ending is by far one of the best endings i've seen in a game and one of the most fun boss battles i have had in the long time, both test and enjoyable.
So on an end not I whole heartly reconmend this game.

A very strong fusion of the roguelike and rhyhtym game genres. Fans of either will be pleased, and fans of both will fall in love.
The game ends up playing like a turn based tactical strategy roguelike where you take 120 turns per minute. While your options and the enemies are never overwhelmingly complex, the real challenge comes from having to think quickly on your feet and to adapt to rapidly changing conditions. It is difficult, and you will die a lot (especially at first), but you will quickly reach a point where the only person you will blame for your deaths will be yourself. Every enemy in the game has a simple movement and attack pattern that will rigidly adhere to, which means when you fail to notice that black skeleton had it's hands up and it kills you, you curse yourself for your mistake, not for the game being cheap.
This feeds into the rhythym element too. Unlike in other rhythym games where hitting arrows in a designer-determined sequence felt more like tapping along to a tune than really dancing, there are no giant arrow prompts on screen telling you what to do. As a result, the more you familiarize yourself with the game, the music, and the levels, you instinctively start to 'feel' where to move and as you reach that point, the game feels more like 'dancing' than any rhythym game has before it. Each zone feels kinesthetically unique, from the back and forth hops in Zone 1, to the konga beat of King Konga.
It's a wonderful game for sitting down and playing for long periods of time, but I've also really enjoyed how easy it is to just launch the game and play a few rounds. The game is technically in early access, but already in a very playable state. There are still features to add (most notably more cutscenes to flesh out the story), but the 3 zones (broken up into 3 levels each) plus 3 bosses already in the game provide a really entertaining challenge as-is and I don't get the feeling of missing core features/mechanics while playing.
Heartily reccomended. I can tell already this game is going to be a big deal; get it now and you can be that cool friend who discovered it first.

If you've never played this game before, now you have to, so long as you're an RPG fan. One of the best Final Fantasy storylines to date (and one of the best RPG storylines in RPG history) is right here with Final Fantasy VII. The story progression evolves in a way that you get a little bit more information as you go along, but not enough to solve the puzzle that is Cloud, your main character.
The gameplay offers much for those needing a break from the storyline. Dozens of sidequests open up ways to get insanely powerful items or to reveal additional backstory details. Mini Games are present, such as Chocobo Racing, to also give you a break from the story while still allowing you to get additional GIL, special chocobos, or rare items.
Often enough you'll find yourself playing the game for hours on end, wanting to find out what will happen next, or what storyline segment will be revealed. The story has so much depth that it will be difficult to follow along during a first playthrough, depending on your play style and pacing.
A must have for RPG fans. A absolute need for Final Fantasy fans. And "this is the one to play" if you're curious about getting into the RPG scene.

Absolutely recommendable FPS experience, with a somewhat steep but highly rewarding learning curve.
I originally backed the development of this game when it moved away from being a mod for the HL1 engine. I tried several beta builds but didn't like it back then. Now, after several years, I took it for a new spin and its great to see how much it has been polished. It is now a solid FPS game.
Dive into the training sessions before you join servers with live players. You'll have much more fun that way, and it won't take more than 15-20 minutes before you have a decent understanding of the game mechanics.
Minor issues which you will have to overlook:

Natural Selection 2 Is a cluster♥♥♥♥ of RTS, FPS, and MOBAs, and I love it.
There's two factions: TSF Marines (the shooty people,) and the Khaara (pretty angery alien chubmonsters.)
Each side has advantages and disadvantages. Thankfully neither are big enough to warrant one side being vastly superior.
As A Marine, you get to shoot guns. Yeah, crazy. You start each life with an Assault Rifle, a Pistol, and a combat toothbrush. Believe it or not, the toothbrush isn't any good on the field. You'll want to upgrade to constantine-barbed floss first thing. You can do this using resources, which you get over time, with you having your own resources to get guns, grenades jetpacks, and exosuits with, and a big amount of resources near the Minimap called "TEAM RESOURCES", for the Commander to use. And here's the main aspect of the marines: Building up your base.
No matter what team you're on, you are lead by a Commander. The commander's job is to place down things like armories, spawnpoints, sentries, teleporters, power nodes, harvesters... basically everything. This is where a big problem can come up, and why I updated my first review:
THE COMMANDER IS A ROLE NO ONE WANTS TO PLAY.
There's a lot of stress, as your decisions heavily affect how the other players are forced to play. If you make a base in the wrong place, make the wrong building, or just have bad timing, you can get screwed big time.
If you love RTS gameplay, then please for the love of god, PLEASE play Commander! It's a role you might love to play, and you'll be doing everyone a favor doing it.
...anyway...
when these little blueprint thingies are put down, they aren't instantly built if you are a Marine. This is because, in RTS fashion, you need people to build them. ...but there are no peasants, no things you can control (at least early), not even a magical robot to do this. Well, you have teammates. As a Commander of the Marines, you need to know the philosophy of TEAMWORK!
Other fellow Marines build your stuff with either welders, or these weird 3-D printing laser guns. This game is totally proletariat-inclined, with the workers being what makes a team a team. But they ain't shooting no Allens without gouns. It's a symbotic relationship if you play as the Marines, with you helping spread the base into further and further regions, in order to get sweet upgrades, like a better machine gun, a flamethrower, a grenade launcher, jetpacks, and the end-all-be-all of the Marines: The Hulking, Unstoppable, Interchangable EXOSUIT.
With the main thing of the Marines being teamwork, the Khaara are totally independent.
As the Khaara, you have one goal, and one goal only: DESTROY AND KILL ALL MARINES AND MARINE BUILDINGS. Without guns, your one weapon is this dinky little bite. It may look weak, but it can actually kill a marine in seconds if you are careless enough to let you get near. Now, we need to get some better bites. This is where the most independent aspect of the Khaara begins. Evolution. As an Alien, you will want to save up resources, in order to evolve. You're probably going to say "well, i'm just going to get something like a tiny bit of armor, or sharper teeth..." and that is where you are WRONG.
The Khaara are a heavily evolved threat. They have evoled to the point where some of them are specialized in very particular ways.
Some prefer to sneak around and assault the Marines behind enemy lines, invisible.
Some defend the mother Hive, spitting corrosive goo and healing the other Aliens.
When you evolve, you have the choice of either upgrading aspects of your current form using resources, or to transform into a different lifeform altogether.
First, there is the Skulk. A small, four-legged creature, with a big bite. Mobile, efficient, and most of all, free.
Next up, there's the Gorge. A chubby little critter. Acidic spit. Healing bile. The ability to construct obstactles for the Marines. And a slide for increased movement.
Third, the Fade. Bipedal. Arms easily seen as scythes. Adaptable hide, allowing for transversal through enemy areas unseen.
Fourth, the aerial Lerk. Evoled arms into wings. A vicious, stinging tail. Horrible, poisonous bites. Clouds of spores to choke out the competition and block ranged attacks.
And there is one that is fairly well known. One with monstrous horns, and fangs feet long. With impressive strength, and armor plating that makes bullets feel like tic-tacs.
The one called the Onos.
All of these mostrosities can be yours, but only if you work for it.
Speaking of work, let's talk about the commander.
As the Alien hive commander, you support your team and spread infestation everywhere.

The gameplay here is weak due to extremely illogical inventory puzzles that only get worse as you near the end, and thus you essentially have to either spend hours trying every possible combination or read a step-by-step guide. The worst is the second acts of the first two parts, and the last act of the last, as they introduce too many items and too many locations at once, overwhelming you and effectively forcing use of a guide. Minigames, which are rather common, are a welcome change of pace, but are still at times nothing but frustration with little reward.
The story is alright, but unfortunately, you play as the worst (most dishonest, sexist, egotistical, immature, narcissistic, and downright unlikable) character in the game. The humor is awful, due in perhaps no small part to a pretty much literal translation from German, as well as extreme repetition of things that were never funny in the first place.
The visuals are great, and are by far the best part of the game.
Steer clear unless the genre itself is sufficient for you.

I'm just going to come right out and say that Hotline Miami is an incredibly good game. And it is a game that you should buy and play for that reason, unless of course you are opposed to the remarkably well done 8-bit Ultra-Violence (yeah, it isn’t about answering phones for the most part).

Hotline Miami is one of those games that kills you over and over, but only because you messed up. Every death is a lesson, or the game calling you out for being lazy and demanding you, to be not perfect, but consistent. And things don’t play out exactly the same even with consistency, so there is that wiggle room for you to react, throw the empty gun at the guy accidently, just stomp his face in before the next guys come around the corner and punch his lights out right before he guts you. Moments like these, where you deviate unexpectedly and make is on luck and reactions leave your heart pounding, especially at the end of a floor, and are intense in a way that was the highlight of the experience.
Another highlight: the music. The music is phenomenal at taking you to the Miami in the 80s with it's just dripping with that neon atmosphere. The music adds so much to the game that I would count going through it without sound as an almost entirely different (and inferior) game. The way it sets the tone is that good.
The story is very surreal and weaves together the levels nicely. The more you know the more you want to know and it is very stingy about giving out particulars. And if after it's done you want more story you can find it at the wiki.
It is well worth a buy at full price, but if there is a sale you have no reason not to pick this game up.

Just finished it... and honestly I'm very mixed.
The entire game had me sitting on the edge of my seat. Throughtout games 1 and 2, and the majority of 3 I was absolutely absorbed, and honestly I could see that a lot of work was put into making the game[s] interesting and exciting (with a couple of rly cool eastereggs).
If I had been asked at anypoint of my playthrough if I would recommend this game (excluding the last hour of so of gameplay) I would have responded "Yes. Definetly, it is one of the best games I've played." but after finishing it, I'm no longer as sure. Other than a very unsatisfying ending that does not fit into the overall genre of the game (which is mostly comedy/sci-fi), the game also leaves huge gaps in knowledge given to the player. One of the biggest sins that a writer can make, is introducing a new concept, a new idea, a new revelation, in the conclusion. And many such things are done within the last hour of game 3. Charectors randomly transforming into each other, things disapearing, things randomly apearing, an overwhelming amount of teleportation, and other things I can't agree with.
Game 1 makes a promise that Rufus will fight his fate with all his might, that his ego, his personality refuses to lose, that he will not be kept down or chained to a planet of filth.
Game 2 makes a promise that Rufus will not hurt those around him, at least not on purpose, (with the exclusion of tricking people into electrocution, that's totally fine for some reason) but It restates that he will not give up, not even when it's hopeless.
Game 3 confuses the everloving crap out of any sort of logic you may try to use. It creates question after question after question, and then instead of giving us some anwsers in a clever and meaningful way (as I had started to expect), it throws an ending that feels pasted on [and not even much like an ending] at us. Even ignoring the heavily unsatisfying ending, Rufus breaks everything that he as a charector stands for, and becomes what would be a true hero, even though it completely contradicts everything that he as a person, and as a charector stood for. He finally decides to give up. No crazy sceme, no sleigh of hand, nothing of what he stood for or represented. Just a flat, boring, cliche hero ending.
"Goodbye Deponia" never really manages to feel like a goodbye. It just feels like I need to open up game 4, even though game 4 does not(and the dev. promised that it will never) exist.
Tl;Dr:
Game 1 - Outstanding 9/10 would play again in several years
Game 2 - Great 8/10 would play again. Introduces lots of new things to keep a long game from getting stale
Game 3 - 4/10; Plot-Twist reveal mid-game actually quite obvious; Ending leaves more questions than it anwsers (and not the good kind); Unsatisfying End
Nevertheless, most certainly worth a try, if only for the jokes and cool animations.
Edit: Post contemplation I realize that the game is perfect the way it is, and that the ending leaves millions of questions, because the anwsers to them don't really matter, and in your head you are allowed to craft your own ending with such amounts of freedom that you are given, however retaining it's motion and impact. This game was the first one I have ever played, that has given me a sleepless night not because of fear, but because of conteplation.
10/10 to the series.

This game is a solid 40 hours-- 1 playthrough. However, since the game delivers on its promise of a branching storyline, it's worth multiple playtrhoughs. If you branch off at a certain point in the game, there's a huge chunk that you're mssing out on-- unlike the way games like Mass Effect, or The Walking Dead (Telltale) where your choices end up leading more or less to the same scenarios. There's an entire arc of characters that are reserved for a different path. The game is also super pretty, the character models being some of the best I've ever seen, and the environments are pretty open. The problem of the game is in some other choices that the devs made-- the gameplay is built around a controller, so m+kb is dumb to play. This really shows in the crappy menus. The quick menu is slow and breaks immersion, the meditation menu is bad. The combat also doesn't make sense without a controller. Some of these things seem like downgrades from The Witcher 1 (which you should play first, screw you if you don't like it). Overall though, the devs have admitted their mistakes and are looking to fix them in TW3, so we'll see. Play TW1 first though.

A very strong fusion of the roguelike and rhyhtym game genres. Fans of either will be pleased, and fans of both will fall in love.
The game ends up playing like a turn based tactical strategy roguelike where you take 120 turns per minute. While your options and the enemies are never overwhelmingly complex, the real challenge comes from having to think quickly on your feet and to adapt to rapidly changing conditions. It is difficult, and you will die a lot (especially at first), but you will quickly reach a point where the only person you will blame for your deaths will be yourself. Every enemy in the game has a simple movement and attack pattern that will rigidly adhere to, which means when you fail to notice that black skeleton had it's hands up and it kills you, you curse yourself for your mistake, not for the game being cheap.
This feeds into the rhythym element too. Unlike in other rhythym games where hitting arrows in a designer-determined sequence felt more like tapping along to a tune than really dancing, there are no giant arrow prompts on screen telling you what to do. As a result, the more you familiarize yourself with the game, the music, and the levels, you instinctively start to 'feel' where to move and as you reach that point, the game feels more like 'dancing' than any rhythym game has before it. Each zone feels kinesthetically unique, from the back and forth hops in Zone 1, to the konga beat of King Konga.
It's a wonderful game for sitting down and playing for long periods of time, but I've also really enjoyed how easy it is to just launch the game and play a few rounds. The game is technically in early access, but already in a very playable state. There are still features to add (most notably more cutscenes to flesh out the story), but the 3 zones (broken up into 3 levels each) plus 3 bosses already in the game provide a really entertaining challenge as-is and I don't get the feeling of missing core features/mechanics while playing.
Heartily reccomended. I can tell already this game is going to be a big deal; get it now and you can be that cool friend who discovered it first.

Infuriating Rom hack!
What I just said sums it up in lots of ways. I have 3 problems with this sequel to one of the most legendary beat 'em ups ever concieved. Most won't agree but I am not looking for others agreement I am just stating my opinion and if you can't respect that at the least then go FLI CK yourself. I'll make this as short as possible.
Problem number 3. Cheaply made complete with cheap deaths.
I am no expert in programming nor do I understand too much in the ways of it but you can tell this game has the originality of a rom hack. There is very little here that is original even for a double dragon game.Most baddies here are clearly just sprite hacks with 4 which appear original but they aren't special You have more platforming in this game than in previous entries.  That within it's self is infiriating and it's worse when there is a enemy as they will hit you and there is nothing you can do. Some times you can land a hit on these goons but most of the time you'll take a hit and fall to your death. If you are lucky you can land a hit before hand but it's a 50/50 chance.  This does not feel like a sequel to me at all as it's just re-used stuff from double dragon 1 and 2. I bet this was made within a month with the unity engine or something along the lines of a web based flash game. Don't believe me? Play "Kung Fu 2" flash game... it's just as simple as this! With little of anything original or note worthy. This game was simply going for people who thrive on nostalgia. While that CAN be a great thing,but you can ruin it if you don't add anything new to something that has been done to death before with recycled everything. There are new moves which are nice but we'll touch on that in a bit. Now on to the next problem.
Problem 2: Sound and Music
This is a huge problem for me as I enjoy nearly all the soundtracks from the Double Dragon saga.There is the Retro mode and remastered mode. The remastered sounds like cheap microsoft wavetable synth while retro is NES sound (I prefer the retro) but *Sigh* This game... as I stated above recycles most of the tunes from previous games, There are "Some" new material here but just like with any game of this era it's uninspired crap! no song that won't get stuck in your head like the previous entries had! (Excluding Neo geo DD and DD  V as I try to pretend those don't exist).You'll hear Stage 1 music from the first game,Theme song of Double Dragon but that's it. What about songs from Super Double Dragon which has a far superior soundtrack? How about some of the memorable tunes from Double Dragon II like the final boss theme or level 1? If you are going to recycle aspects of previous games at least put NOTE WORTHY tunes.might as well recycle ALL the songs (unless under copyright...maybe that's why ) Sound effects....Recycled. Nothing new, heard it before. As I said ROM HACK or Flash based cash grab. Thanks alot,guys! Now the final problem *crack knuckles*.
Problem number one - Overall gameplay,Combat and Collision detection.
Oh boy. Where does one start? Double Dragon isn't what I would call brilliant but it's legendary as it was one of the first beat 'em ups that was fun,was co-op and had awesome martial art type moves that was amazing to see at the time. Fun music to tap your toe too and of course game play that was unmatched by any standard. This is where Double Dragon IV biggest problem lies. The combat is horribly flawed in ways I can't even explain. Double Dragon is beat dudes up and move on. This one you have to be careful on how you attack enemies or they will jump kick you to the point where you can't get up to fight back unless you die! Sure, "SOMETIMES" you can do the upper cut and rising kick to recover like you could in Double Dragon II: The Revenge but the other issue arises is the bloody collision detection! I am a veteren of this series and know how the hurricane kick works and I can tell you that it will barely make any contact with enemies unless they are pixel perfect toe to toe with you. Same with the upper cut and rising knee. There are some new moves that look awesome.One is like a vertical barrel roll and a similar side kick like in the original game and they do great damage IF YOU CAN CONNECT THEM! This "KILLS" the game as if the other issues weren't bad enough. Did I mention the enemies have specials too? Yep. Abobo is horribly unbalanced when you fight the green and black one. He'll do a "Jumping vertical arm bar" and all your health goes bye-bye. You can,like in previous entries,spam the elbow attack which is no fun. why go through the entire game by doing one move to make it playable enough to be able to continue? It's rubbish!

I have always wanted to get the individual games, but given that 3 in a series is quite an investment, and since I could never figure if I would really enjoy the game from what I saw from the trailer, it took me quite some time to decide to finally obtain this game.
Pros:
If you enjoy point and click adventures with challenging puzzles interspersed in the midst of storytelling, this game should be for you.
Entertaining characters whom you will get close to
A rich environment that really encourages exploration.
A sense of humor that I would describe as a sarcastic poke at the main character, who almost seems to always receive the brunt of things
The achievements are really fun to figure out. (There are tons of them!)
A useful (very useful!) save system
Cons:
Not a serious issue, but I am someone who gets slightly frustrated easily, so trying to figure out which of 10 items goes where and with what can get slightly nerve wracking. I simply just look at a walkthrough if I hit a wall, which allows me to still follow the story without getting too frustrated, but if you enjoy challenges, then don't, because it is worth slowly figuring out
This new 3 in 1 package features the developer commentary, which you can turn off, but it automatically switches on every time the game starts. It is not terribly obstructive in the top left corner, so its still a small complaint.
No spoilers, but some people may be terribly hurt by the ending of this if they don't like it. Personally though, I liked the ending, and I find it the most meaningful out of any other ending they could have placed.
Other than the minor cons, this game does promise a nice storyline, a brisk fun walk with the characters and amazing environments. It is a different style of game but is worth going through all 3. :)

This isn't the first point-and-click adventure I've played, but it won't certianly be my last.
This was probably the most enjoyable game i've ever played, sinking 17 hours into it over three days.
As seen in the title, this is the complete journey including Deponia 1, Deponia 2, and Deponia 3. As such, I'll be doing 3 small reviews, based on each game.
Deponia:
This is the first game, as you've probaby learned. It's got a bit of a corny feel in the beginning, but I quickly grew to like it, and understood that this game is not meant to be serious. It's got plenty of interesting characters, locations, and some great voice actors. While this game is pretty difficult after the first area, and I'm not ashamed to admit I used a walkthrough in alot of the game, I can see where it would be possible without them. It leaves off to a mediocre ending, but with the money gained from this, the company made the next two games brilliant.
Deponia 2:
With better cutscenes, music, writing and etc., It's a great sequel. With brilliant artwork, It kept me entranced, even through the slump that most media goes through in the middle episode. It keeps you excited from the very beginning, and kept me excited until the very end.
Deponia 3:
It's better in every way than either of the previous games. It's hard for me to talk about much without revealing the ending, plot twists, or anything really. It's an amazing game. Play all of them.
Overall:
These games are beautiful, immense, and deep. They are worth the price, and I am probably going to do another playthrough, listening to the developer commentary. Also, those "Huzza!" transitions are pretty amazing.

is a trilogy of old-school point-and-click adventure games, all wrapped into a single executable file for your convinience.
The story revolves around Rufus, a self-proclaimed genius, a tinkerer, who lives on planet Deponia, covered with trash (
is a German word for
). One day, he tries to put into motion another one of his plans to reach Elysium (a
that is hovering above Deponia and where lives the elite). But (of course) his plan fails again and results in Goal, an Elysian girl, falling down to the surface of Deponia. The rest is about the misadventures of Rufus, Goal, several reccuring characters - how they try to get back to Elysium and what discoveries they make in the process.
I found the jokes in this game to be absolutely hilarious, however that depends on whether you like crass and dark humor or not - there's quite a lot of such humor. And not only the dialogue is funny, the animated sequences contain some funny slapstick situations as well. There are a few (like, a dozen for the whole 30+hrs trilogy) swearwords (which I did not expect), but who cares?
The voice acting (both English and German) is top-notch. I prefer German voiceover, but the English one is just as good - I switched back and forth b/w them a couple of times.
The game is very beautiful, that is if you are willing to overlook low-budget animation drawbacks - sometimes you can feel that there is not enough frames drawn for this or that action to look satisfying. The backgrounds are absolutely gorgeous though.
The puzzles in this game are satisfiyngly difficult, for the most part, which is a good thing. Some of them were, however illogical (like the one with the Yrk and the paper plane, or the one involving the conveyor belt
). This is a minor drawback. but still I had to look in the guide a couple of times. For the most part though, the puzzles are creative and you just need to think harder to solve them. A lot of interesting minigames are there as well.
This edition could use some more polish, the game freezed on me a couple of times, which lead to some loss of progress. However not much progress was lost in either case, the game autosaves at important plot points by itself - just make sure to click 'Continue' and not load your last savegame. The text boxes for the commentary sometimes shifts to the right part of the screen, instead of a text box frame. But those are all minor drawbacks, which I am sure will be fixed with a patch.
The community seems to be split about the ending, however I find it brilliant and very cleverly written.
Overall, it's a very enjoyable adventure with a great story, great humor, brilliant plot twists and smart puzzles. I recommend it to any point-and-click adventures enthusiast.

So here is my review on this game. I was a bit confused when I first bought this game. EVERY review said this game was trash, worthless and not even worth playing even if it was free. Almost all reviews gave this game a 1/10, but since it was only 99 cents I figured why not give it a try.
Then I started to play it with a friend of mine and I was amazed! It uses the unreal engine so it lacks graphics. Also the physics are quite terrible. However, if you look at the other aspects of this game, this is probably the most amazing zerg game that exists.
The game offers A LOT of achievements. For every achievement run player this game is worth it even if it was 10 euro's. It offers great co-op gameplay with many different gameplay options. It's like risk or rain for example. The graphics are terrible but the game offers a system that makes it fun to replay the game, get achievements, unlock abilities and progress every run. For everyone that is not a graphics or storyplayer (read casual), this game is a MUST buy!
One big thing with this game is the online play. So many people hate it and don't understand the great features of this game that the online play lacks quite a bit. It's hard to find a proper server with random people, so it's easier to play with people you know. I must agree, this game certainly isn't the best game in several aspects, but I'm still able to get a great amount of fun with the replay system. Get achievement, level you character and progress every time you restart a map.
Also, another great thing about this game is the updates. DLC? What is dlc? ORION doesn't know the term DLC. If you buy this game you don't buy half a game that gets filled with "updates" like most games. "You want to have additional maps or weapons? Sure, but you'll have to pay us another 5 euro's to get those items." A normal way of selling a products in the game industry these days. ORION doesn't give a s**t. This is probably the most updated game there is atm and it won't cost you a single dime. It's all FREE, like it always was, until someone decided that everything had to be paid for. This is a complete game and it grows bigger every time there's an update. It might not be popular, but atleast ORION is a company that cares about their product, rather then screwing over the player base.
Overall, this game gives a great amount of fun. Don't buy this game if you are either a casual, a storyline based player or a player that requires good graphics. For everyone else and especially the hardcore gamer that likes to complete the full game (100%, progress runs) this game is highly recommended.

Double Dragon's a series that's been around for 30 years, and I guess this is some sort of tribute to the 30th anniversary. What we've got is a "retro revival" sort of deal that's continuing on from a specific branch of the games; that being the NES trilogy. That particular set of console ports is beloved by many who grew up in the NES era, and it's that exact aesthetic that Double Dragon 4 evokes. More specifically, it's the aesthetic of Double Dragon 2. The look and feel of this game is not unlike that one, with many of the sprites looking like they were taken straight from it. With the benefit of hindsight, the NES trilogy was not without its flaws. Double Dragon 4 patches over some of these; the limitation of needing to hit both face buttons on an NES controller to jump is replaced with a dedicated jump, which is helpful. Additional buttons can be mapped for extra attacks like a roundhouse kick or elbow, and they'll help.
The game's not all that hard, and gives you three lives and five credits to beat the whole thing. This can't be changed in any way, nor is there much of a difficulty selection. I made it to the last boss on one 50-minute playthrough, found a new move in the help menu, and all but steamrolled through again on that second playthrough to clear it in just under two hours. Replay value is limited, but there in a fashion; you have 2-player co-op and duel modes, as well as a Tower mode that's just a survival gauntlet against 100 waves of enemies. Progress in the latter unlocks new characters for the story mode, so if you wanted to go through the game as one of the enemies, you can. In the end, it's okay. $7 USD is not that bad of an asking price for it if you're super nostalgic for Double Dragon 2 on NES and want something that evokes that. If you have the extra money, Double Dragon Neon would also scratch that itch and give you a bit more bang for your buck, but this is just fine. It's okay, which is perfectly fitting considering that the NES trilogy was pretty okay for the most part as well.

Essentially a slapdash clone of NES Double Dragon 2. It's not very good. What follows will be a stream of consciousness airing of grievances:
The default music is quite bad, but the Retro music is totally fine. Not sure why this is even an option given that the game is pretending to be 8-bit.
The background visuals are almost entirely drawings or even photos clumsily reduced to lower color depth, rather than actual pixel art. With one or two exceptions they look very poor and clash with the sprites. The font used in the pointless cutscenes looks a lot like the default text tool font from Microsoft Paint.
Mission design is extremely basic, lacking in verticality or any kind of interesting traversal. Move to the right a screen or two, maybe climb a ladder, then wait an uncomfortably long time for enemies to walk on screen once scrolling stops.
No setpieces to speak of. There's a floating platform in stage 1 that just sticks you in place while it moves to the right for like 10 seconds. Were there supposed to be enemies here?? There's an elevator sequence where you just fight a single Abobo--compare that to the elevator in stage 1 of Super DD. There's nothing like the helicopter level. Nothing like the bulldozer fight. Trap/platforming sequences are arbitrarily placed and thoughtlessly put together.
The first 2/3rds of story mode is a complete joke. You may die once or twice from a pit or spikes. It's difficult to even take damage from the basic enemies--until the final stages you're never in situations that are frantic or require thought. Ultimately all of my deaths came from either traps or fast single boss attacks that took 80% off my life bar.
The combat is "OK" but for as padded out as the game is there's not a large enough variety of moves. Mostly you just spam special attacks or abuse z-movement to start combos. I found myself constantly wishing for a stomp or something to attack downed enemies. Weapons are very sparse and feel very bad--the knife bounces off people?? Enemies seem mostly unable to access the very bottom or very top of any given screen, strangely, so you almost always have a safe zone.
Tower mode is just a slapped together survival mode added as another way to gate unlock characters. Ridiculously basic and a slog. All the normal game's problems except you're fighting two or three enemies at a time, 100 times.
It's cheap, at least, but that is definitely a reflection of the effort and pride that went into development.

Defcon is a simple looking yet complex game of strategy. From the beginning you must place resources and units around the map to determine your defense game. Cluster resources or spread them out? Defend heavily populated cities first or risk losing protection for more coverage? Deploy fleets in the Atlantic or the Pacific? Each defending each area has its own unique challenges to overcome which can make for a huge amount of strategies and layouts that anybody can test.
Beyond the gameplay is the atmosphere. The very basic graphics evoke the feeling of being in a war room straight out of the movie WarGames and the slow sad music, ambient sounds of orders slowly and carefully given through the room, a weeping woman in the corner, the sound of The Lords Prayer softly played over the loudspeaker, and the low hum whenever a nuke explodes makes you feel the sheer magnitude of everything you are witnessing. You are watching the world die and YOU are making it happen. Seeing a town you grew up in disappear in a flash of light and reading the tally of the dead is downright soul-crushing.
Over all this is a very experiential and fun game for LAN parties. The only problem is that online matchmaking takes forever because of a small community. Otherwise this game is very strategic, very fun, and hauntingly beautiful.
If you're looking for a good throwback game that reminds us how frustratingly hard our old games were then this game is a must have.

I prefer to write detailed reviews where possible, talking about pro's, con's, what I liked and what I didn't like.
For this game, however, it simply isn't possible. I'm not a console player, and I don't have a controller lying around, and I found that with a mouse and keyboard this game is basically unplayable.
For an action-y game, with precise controls required, the lazy-console-port which resulted in mapping the movement pad straight to WASD (meaning that you only have 8 direction of motion) certainly has a lot of non-8-direction movements required.
It's poorly thought out, poorly implemented and unintuitive. Simply implementing the standard top-down-shooter mechanics of W=towards mouse, S=away from mouse and A/D=strafe would've been a significant improvement. This is not complex or ground-breaking stuff. It's a rookie mistake by a rookie developer and it kills what could've been an awesome game.
[edit]I have uninstalled the game and requested a refund. If the devs ever get around to implementing a decent control scheme, however, I will certainly reconsider this game because it looks great. It's just unplayable.[/edit]

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn Of war: Dark Crusade: Black Scuffle is pretty cool I guess.
Set in the distant future of the 41st Mellenia, Mankind has decided to show aliens just whos the boss of this gym by beating them all up. 10,000 years after their Jesus figure got cripple, humanity now has to fight an endless war across the stars for total domination against aliens and other humans that don't like them very much.
The planet Kronus, located on the edge of an alien empire known as the Tau, has suddenly been thrown into an all out war between numerous different factions.
The Tau themselves, a highly advanced alien race that relies on ranged weaponry and the help of other aliens for close combat, basically the nerds of the 40k world.
The Imperial Guard, regular humans who fight with flash lights and balls of titanium. They also have big tanks and scary men who wear cool hats.
The Eldar space elves who think they're smart but actually aren't. They also accidentally spawned a chaos god a few thousand years ago because they wouldn't stop having planetary scale murder orgies.  So like they're ones to talk about short comings of other races.
They suck, I hate them.
The Necrons, grumpy robot skeletons who were awoken because of all the gosh dang racket going on up stairs. Now want to destroy all life.
Orks, space fungus soccer hooligans that can't stop shooting and punching everything. They're fun guys to be around.
The forces of Chaos, evil humans that worship the gods of Chaos. Like to summon daemons (it's spelled like that in game) and get into bar fights. They're jerks.
And of course there are the poster boys, the Space Marines, roided up super jocks that are like 8 feet tall and poop pure rage.
Each race battles for control of the planet, trying to accomplish their own goals and thwart the plans of others by sitting down and discussing the matter like civil adults.
I made that up. They kill each other hardcore.
Now, I bought this game at launch, over the years I've accumulated about a hundred hours or so all together and only recently got a CD key from Sega for the steam version after Relic servers shut down.
Dawn of war is more or less a traditional style RTS with a focus on base building. It's big thing is that your main resource comes from nodes you need to capture and secure on the map instead of building farms or something like that. This means that there is always a threat of combat as your enemies head out and attempt take points from you, furthering their resource gain while crippling yours. It's an aggressive way of playing that makes you constantly push your units forward instead of just turtling in your base.
There is also a toggle for most units that lets them switch between ranged combat and melee combat, giving you another layer of strategy. There are units that specialize in ranged combat and units that specialize in giving wedgies and shoving you in a locker. It adds another layer of strategy as how to build your army. Your firewarriors may have a powerful ranged attack, but sooner or later those angry green rioters are going to reach your firing line, and then you'll look silly. Good thing you have these goofy bird looking guys that like to hit things with sticks, so you can happily fire away while your Kroot friends literally eat their enemies.  Gross.
Single player is actually pretty neat. Instead of having a mission to mission story, you instead fight over the planet in a risk-style fashion. Each army has a pre-set number of locations where they can use points to reinforce their territory and buy special units for their army. While it can get kind of dull fighting for the same territory, it makes up for it with the stronghold missions of each faction acting like a more traditional kind of RTS mission.
The voice acting is...Pretty friggin great. It's like a bunch of Shakespearean B-actors yelling mad banter at one another.
This all being said, should you play Dim Expedition?
It's pretty great, it adds a bunch of stuff to the last two games while also having a really neat competitive aspect in the form of multiplayer. If you can get it on the cheap, you should do so, but chances are you already have this game, considering how old it is.

Starting out as a lowly apprentice barely able to cast a fire ball and eventually build up to creating truly complex spells that can then in turn cast other more complex spells was a blast. That and the somewhat rock paper scissors approach to magic and resistance meant that you would be challenged by each new enemy type to create a new spell to counter their element and attack pattern.
Not that you even need get that focused if you didn’t want to.
Basic spells work well and I frequently made spells up for fun to just to throw them at enemies to see what worked or was most visually stunning; Like my lightning storm that created frost and tornados that created yet more lightning.
This came in handy as the optional puzzles often ask you to make a spell work in ways you don’t think of during normal fights allowing you to bring that creativity to other parts of the game when they reward you with new spells or modifiers.
Outside of the magic crafting system Mages is a fun Zelda like game. If you enjoy a decent, if somewhat basic, story about magic, creative spell creation as well as the chaos that sometimes brings I’d recommend Mages of Mystralia.

Hi all, nukes here.
Natural Selection 2
is a multiplayer team orientated game.
Like most stories there are two sides to each.
is just that, one side is the first person shooter and the other is the commanding side top down real time strategy, with real life units the best kind of unit.. right? More detail on this later.
In
teams are pitted against each other humans
versus aliens
both teams battle it out over strategic resources, over a range of very different maps. Till there is only one team left able to fight.
I found this game to be right up my alley loving the tactical aspects as well as the strategies. Please keep in mind a majority of the player base have played for well over 500+ hours and many of them have no patience for newcomers all though some are very welcoming and have time to teach.
Bearing that in mind I'll delve deeper into why I personally think this is a great game.
Before you jump eagerly jump into the multiplayer servers, the game will urge you to play the tutorials
and I can strongly recommend this as back in my day when I first started this game I never had the chance.
The tutorials will cover all basic aspects of the game such as marines, aliens and commanding. This does not include skill, which my friend is up to you and a bit of practice.
Also knowing a map goes a long way. I still get lost... like a lot.
So before I mentioned that this game has two sides the
and the
Commanding side.
This game can be very difficult, lucky for new comers the first 5 levels of your personal character enable you to join rookie servers where only rookies are allowed to play.

Once you have grown past level 5 unfortunately those servers are inaccessible to you. Meaning you have to join the big boys.
Practice, practice, practice... or just die a lot like I did, gritting your teeth at every turn.
NS2 is a keyboard and mouse based game, if you are use to FPS games or RTS game the controls are relatively straight forward and easy to pick up.
If you are not happy with the bindings you are able to change them in the options.
The achievements on this game are fairly straight forward although there will be a few that are difficult to acquire.
There are no achievements that have sapped the fun out of it for me.
There is no unfolding story to this game unfortunately and there is no single player campaign mode.
Although there is single player horde mode and tutorials.
The combat is all real time so you had better check those corners before you run out into the open.
You never know what maybe lurking in the dark above you.
Marines -
Aliens -
There is no skill and trait system, there is a personal level system that works off exp gained from playing online.
Online players also have a Hive skill score which relates to how well you play globally.
The aliens however work differently from the marines while in a match. You as an alien may evolve and select different traits based on which hive the commander has chosen. Multiple hives means multiple choices.
As an alien you may evolve
in to other roles that have similarities as support
, assassin
, tank
and flying nuisance... the
.
Sounds are relative to the game and can be adjusted nicely into the menus. I found all the sounds suit the environment and had no issues.
The graphics are very pleasant, first time rending can take some time, but the game has been optimised greatly.
Everyone loves a cute gorge right? Well its regarded in the community that the gorge is cute I don't see it myself but something to do with the ears?
Also "T" to taunt in game.
The steam workshop is available for this game and NS2 has a good community that produce mods and maps. Many of the top servers have been heavily modded so first time loading may take some time, but mods such as NS2+ options are totally worth the weight.
NS2+ means you can play around with your heads up display
look and also vision options for aliens and much more.
This game is orientated to multiplayer and the single play modes are really just the tutorials and horde mode.
Although some servers are hosted with bot teams so you can practice and there is also arcade modes that will present different challenges.
I haven't come into any game breaking bugs myself.
I would say one of the only draw backs is that some of the loads screens can take a while. Especially if you are joining a new server for the first time with added mods. As upon joining the mods will download for the first time.
Patience is a virtue.
So a lengthy review, that I hoped I covered all the bases . I personally enjoy this game on many different levels as I love RTS games and FPS although I am a terrible shot.
This a good all round game for FPS and RTS lovers. If you like killing aliens or hiding in a corner stalking your prey, until the time is right to slice and dice then I hope you will enjoy this game as much as me.

Fantastic game blending FPS and RTS.  Not only that, but the teams use asymmetric tactics yet are pretty equal in their strengths.
Marines focus on long-range combat and require a tighter degree of teamwork than the alien team.  This allows a team which works together well and have goal-oriented players to do far better than a team whose players focus on trivial things like KDRs or use disharmonous tactics.  Teamwork also allows Marines to effectively utilize powerful late-game tech like exo-suits which require support marines to repair them as well as concentrating the firepower needed to take down the Onos or Fades.
The Aliens focus primarily upon melee combat, though there are exceptions.  Aliens can operate a little more independently than Marines in the later stages of the round when higher lifeforms like Fades and Lurks.  Onos usually require a gorge to heal them or a commander prescient enough to build forward bases and a team to defend them.
The Marine commander is a bit more challenging than the Alien commander, too, due to the amount of micro-managing of support, but this also allows the commander to be quite a bit more effective than the Alien commander as the Marine commander does not need to build structures in order to heal Marines or resupply their ammo.  This is powerful early game, but forward bases are still recommended mid-late game.
Overall, many, many hours of fun to be had with this game.  The only recommendation is doing some training before taking the commander's chair.

Crypt is a dungeon crawler, but with a twist. That twist being moving to the beat of awesome electronic music by the amazing Danny Brananowsky (Who also worked on Binding of Issac's and Super Meat Boy's music, so have high expectations.)
...No literally, you MOVE to the beat. So do the monsters. That's what I like about this game, you got to keep with the rhythm of the game while you're simultaniously exploring the cave and seeing what you can get. It's two genres I couldn't think be combined, but it works beautifully. You have entities like health, and item slots for armor and weapon and magic, etc. However, the whole gameplay is composed of moving around to the soundtrack.
It's exciting keeping your mind on two things at once, and mastering it in the end. Enemies all have their own movement patterns according to the music, so you're not the only one that has to deal with the beat. I must admit it's very exhilirating to learn every little bit of enemy movement, and gracefully going through the dungeon with the head bopping tunes in your head.
However, if you wanna add your own music to the mix, you can! Any MP3 file you have can be implimented in the game. Experiment, and see what you get.
Overall, this game is tons of fun, and is looking to be one of my favorite indie games out there. I'm not even that big a fan of dungeon crawlers, but I'm a sucker for rhythm games. I HIGHLY recommend this to anyone looking for a good, repetitive time.

Alot of people call it an Overwatch clone. Alot of people call Overwatch a Paladins clsone.
Both are not true!
The two games do have some similarities, but then again, they both did not invent fps, they both did not invent Assault/Escort/Payload mode, they both did not invent MoBa Style Gameplay and they both did not invent lootboxes for sure.
But what makes both games unique and what gives them both the right to exist?
Well, let me point out some things: (This is more from the PoV of Paladins, as it is a Paladins review)
1. Paladins is fully free 2 play where Overwatch is buy 2 play.
So in Paladins you start out with a few free champions and you can unlock more and more over time with ingame credits, additionally you can unlock all the content at once by buying "the game" just like if you buy Overwatch.
2. Paladins is played 5v5 where Overwatch is played 6v6, so you could say in Paladins each individual player has a little more responsibility.
3. Paladins has a more tactical feel when selecting your champions compared to Overwatch, as it is possible to change your heroes in Overwatch at any time. To be honest, both systems feel right & wrong at times. Means sometimes you wish you could switch your champion in Paladins during the game when you notice that you misspicked, and vice versa in Overwatch you sometimes have the feeling your opponent can adapt to fast to a specific setup and just change their roster on the fly.
I can not really say one of the two systems is better or not, this really comes down to personal taste I guess.
4. Paladins has something that Overwatch does not have, the burn cards and the upgrades. The burn cards give you the possibilitly to select a set of cards altering the abilities of your champions to some extent. The upgrades give you the possibility to boost your champion during the game a bit relying on your own (and your teams) performance, meaning the better you are playing the better upgrades you can get.
5. Paladins lacks map detail and map quantity, where Overwatch really put a lot of love into detail and story hints on the maps, Paladins feels very plain and simple. This does not have to be a straight minus though, as adding more details to maps could go at the expense of performance. There will I am sure Paladins will be releasing more maps so the quantitiy shouldn't be a big bummer.
So in general, I would say the fact that you can not change your champion during a round and you have the possibility to boost your champion with items during a round gives Paladins a little more of a "MOBA" feeling compared to Overwatch.
Overwatch on the other hand feels more polished and has the Blizzard high standard and balance feel to it.
I do not see a reason why one would have to decide which one is better, I play both and I enjoy both.
As Paladins if fully free to play without any drawback, you do not do anything wrong checking this game out and playing a few rounds!

The Skinny
Double Dragon IV is almost the exact sequel I've been hoping for. It ticks almost every single box one could hope for in a sequel to the legendary Double Dragon II for NES, and does a very competent and solid job of following up such a classic.
The Negatives
The only downsides are that the game is not particularily creative in the way Double Dragon II was, and doesn't build on DDII in much of any meaningful way, outside of adding a battle mode. It also has a cheesy, throw away joke of a storyline, and doesn't feature any memorable new cinematics, like the opening to the original Double Dragon.
The Rest of the Positives
It does however, add some good new enemies, bring the player to some very cool new locations, and present a very fun old school beat em up, with good level design (something we never see in the boring, flat levels of modern beat em ups), and the game ramps up in challenge towards the end in a nice way.
The Takeaway(I like it, and I want more!)
Highly reccomended for old School Double Dragon fans, especially if you were a fan of 2, and would love more game in that vein. Bring on Double Dragon V (or would it be VI?), and truly bring the creativity, more new enemies, more new weapons, and crazier set pieces guys!

Hotline miami is a fantastic game period. Everything about it is fantastic from the gameplay to the music there is nothing this game had done that had left a sour taste in my mouth once i had finished it.
I first want to talk about the soundtrack and how wonderful it is, from making the mood of the game go from electrified and fast paced to somber and tense. This games music all is all presented in an almost synth wave style but the scope of what the music can do is incredible from a jazzy more relaxed song during times of rest, to fast paced and upbeat songs playing during segments of action. Each song does something to contribute to the overall mood of the game, and nothing feels out of place when playing.
The combat in this game boils down to one word, intense. The fast paced gunplay keeps you on the edge of your seat as you clear floor after floor of enemies. The difficulty is high but fair as most of your failures while playing are your own fault. One thing that i enjoyed about this game a lot is the player health or lack thereof. You have the same amount of health as the average enemy forcing you to evolve and change your playstyle when facing lots of enemies at the same time, but when you do eventually die you can instantly get right back into the action.
The environments in this game are simplistic but they do their job in continuing the pacing of the game or in some cases slowing it down. The game will slow down after each level to give time for the player to breath and collect their thoughts, as you go from stores back to the main character's home to where you are thrown right back into the action.
My final topic i would like to write about is the story. The main story involves a organization known as 50 blessings forcing people to commit grisly murders to weaken the american russian peace, and attempting to shape america to its will. The story is very cryptic and complex to piece together due to the events of the game being told through two unreliable narrators "Jacket" and "Biker". Jacket is a unstable character and will often times be unable to determine reality from hallucination because of multiple factors like him being a sociopath, having ptsd (hinted at in hotline miami 2) and *spoilers* re living through many events in the game while in a coma. Biker is an unreliable source of information as most of his key missions that attribute to the story where after drug and alcohol fueled parties.

Hotline Miami is one of my favorite indie games ever made.
A perfect synthesis of design, aesthetic, audio, and atmosphere. Described simply, it is a series of difficult combat challenges that play out from a top down perspective, where you use close and long ranged weapons to dispatch your enemies as quickly and efficiently as you can. Described complexly, it is a cocaine fueled, pulse pounding, neon blasting, hazy fever dream of an experience that anyone who likes good music and fast paced, challenging gameplay should try out.
Enemies all die in one hit, but so do you, so expect to die a lot. The “retry” button is bound to R, so expect to be pressing R as often as you do in an FPS to reload. There are different masks to unlock, which give you different abilities, and a weird, psychedelic surreal storyline to uncover.
This game sits in my definition of a “Perfect Game” where all the mechanics, graphics, controls, and soundtrack come together impeccably, with every component in harmony and nothing contradicting each other. There is literally nothing wrong with the game.
Actually no I lied, a small nitpick would be the enemies shooting you through glass panels on some later levels can get a bit tedious.

Let me get this straight: this is a driving/simulation game like no other! I haven't seen mud simulation like this in any other game. This game looks amazing, and driving those trucks is a lot of fun!
Why am I not recommending this game? Well, mostly due to UX issues:
- No tutorial. You need to look elsewhere to learn the very basics of playing this game.
- Lackluster manual. Sure, the provided manual (in PDF format) looks great, and feels like the paper booklets that came with games in 2000s (remember when games came in a box?). However, it fails to explain several game controls and mechanics.
- Almost-always-online DRM. If you are playing the single-player mode and your connection goes down,
. Fortunately, launching Steam in offline mode works. Also, the game automatically saves the progress on your machine. Which makes me wonder why the developers added such inconvenience.
- Camera controls are annoying. Controlling the camera with the xbox360 gamepad is annoying. Controlling with the mouse is slightly better, but still very annoying.
- Changing gears is too difficult. Trying to shift to the low-gear using the gamepad is nigh impossible. The weird gear layout and poor control with the analog stick makes it a frustrating experience. Changing gears with the mouse is way easier, but still annoying and somewhat pointless.
- You still need the mouse even when using a gamepad or the keyboard. There are several in-game locations that need to be clicked (attach points for winch, trailers and addons management, spawning logs at kiosks, unloading logs).
- "Position your truck properly". You will receive your message when you try to attach trailers to your truck at the garage. Much more frustrating is receiving it when trying to load logs onto the trailer. Intuitively, the truck seems in a good position, but unless both the truck and the trailer are 100% straight, you can't load the cargo. The in-game feedback is poor as well,
. [What should have happened: the trailer should be loaded even if the truck is not straight.]
- The "advanced" UI is a pain to use with the gamepad (I gave up and went for the mouse instead). It is required for controlling the crane and when using the winch with another truck.
- The fuel stations will only refuel a truck if it is at a very specific spot inside the large rectangle. And, maybe, only when using one of the camera modes.
- When spawning logs on the log kiosk, those logs are "tied" to a specific truck. What happened: I had two trucks near a kiosk, one of them had the crane. Then I clicked the button to spawn some logs and tried to load those logs onto the second trailer. Wrong. It did not work. The game wanted me to load those logs onto the first truck. Then I moved the trucks around, changed to the second truck, and finally spawned the logs. But then, those logs were tied either to the back of the truck or to the trailer (choosen at the UI, when clicking). Before loading those logs, of course I had to switch back to the first truck (with the crane). [What should have happened: the game should detect any kind of log on any kind of carriage. The way it was implemented was a shortcut to make the game easier to code, but makes no sense to the player.]
----
This game is fun, driving through the terrain is fun, but all those UX issues distract me from the main game. And those issues happen so often that I can't feel immersed in the game world. [For comparison, Euro Truck Simulator 2 has excellent UX.]
If you want to feel how the game plays, try to download the "tech demo" they released way before the game was ready.
If you think you can cope with those UX issues, go ahead and buy this game!

This game was probably one of my worst buy decisions in all of my time here on steam. If you are thinking about buying this game, please at least listen to what I have to say first.
The game is essentially a literal dungeon runner. Your character dashes at high speed through the dungeon, gaining gold, experience, wood, and stone. Experience is used to buy small upgrades for the character that are more like small changes in game mechanics. Wood and stone are used to repair and upgrade buildings.
Basically the game is similar to Puzzle Quest if you've ever played it, basic match three or more. Unfortunately, the game starts to get increasingly more difficult as the levels progress. The entire difficulty curve is broken. I have often sat for a long stretch in front of a chest desperately trying to get a key match to unlock it only to have the game absolutely refuse to generate keys. What started out as a hopeful adventure then quickly turned into needless frustration. Clearly the developers should have spent more time to ensure that these issues wouldn't crop up. Adding these up makes the game incredibly difficult, however this is all "invisible" difficulty, stuff that is a part of the game mechanics itself that doesn't really add any actual challenge based on skill. I was unable to make it very far due to these frustrating issues. This was very disappointing because I have wanted this game for a very long time and when I finally got the chance to play it, I was rewarded for supporting the game with my money, with a completely arduous task that doesn't actually provide a challenge based on the player's skill. For this reason I would suggest you avoid this game, though it looks nice, plays nice, and is fun at first, it quickly turns out to be frustrating and devolves into a state of madness beyond any hope of repair.

I don't normally play First Person Shooters, but this is an exception! Natural Selection two is a First Person Shooter/Real Time Strategy game. There are two sides: Aliens and Marines. Both sides have unique elements that separate them from the other faction. Each faction has their own commander. All of the players, aside from the commanders, are essentially playing a FPS. The commanders, however, are playing a RTS. The commander, as the name states, tells the other players what to do. The other players are not forced to do what the commander says, so this is a very team-oriented game. The commander also researches upgrades for the other players and can build structures. Being a commander requires a lot of knowledge about the game, so I wouldn't recommend being the commander until you have at least a general understanding of the game.
The goal isn't to get as many kills in a certain period of time; instead, each side needs to destroy the other's base. Most games last 30-50 minutes, and there are no penalties for leaving early. Players can also join a game mid-way through. In my eyes, this is a pro since I don't always have the time to play an entire game. I feel like this game was exceptionally well done and offers a unique concept that keeps me coming back for more.

Deponia is one of the best point'n'clicks I have played in a long time. Its puzzles are reminiscent of the old Monkey Island games, and the humour is without a doubt one of the best of the past 10 years. You play the anti-hero Rufus. As the reviews and intro state, Rufus is not a pleasant man. He's annoying, mean, and absolutely self-centered. The game made me wonder what was wrong with the protagonist several times at the start of the game. He sells women into slavery and feeds children to monsters. And, in spite of all this, he grows on you. He's human. He does horrible things but you still want him to succeed in his plans. Rufus is brilliant, and he's utterly fascinating.
Get this game if you want an interesting protagonist. He won't be your immediate hero. He won't be the man you hope to be, or the man you want your daughter to marry. He's definitely not the man you hope to snag in a relationship. But he will be interesting from start to finish. And that's sorely lacking from games nowadays. So, buy this game and support these makers. You'll be laughing from start to finish.

For a game that's still in Early Access, this is a remarkably satisfying and complete-feeling game.
It's a traditional, 2D-grid-based roguelike, but with the novel restriction that you MUST take an action on every beat of the music or lose your "groove chain", costing you crucial gold. In roguelike platformers (which I love, don't get me wrong), the 20-health-to-instant-death moment is usually caused by you failing to judge a jump or projectile's trajectory by a tiny margin. Here it's simply that you didn't think fast enough. Of course the red dragon was going to breathe fire there. You KNEW that. You just didn't process in time. Next run!
The weapons, shops, shrines, and enemies are well-designed and give the game plenty of variety, and the choice of two major modes (normal, where you use diamonds retrieved from each run to give yourself some advantages or unlock possible items for random drops for future runs, and hardcore, where these starting advantages are forbidden but all items are unlocked to drop from the very beginning) allows players to get into the swing of things in a slightly friendlier manner before attempting hardcore run after hardcore run.
