A nice change of pace from what most driving games offer nowadays.  Rather than just wreckless driving, you're actually given an objective using big, old-school russian logging vehicles, with secondary objectives that aren't needed, but help quite a bit with moving back and forth from the log dumps to the yard.
Casual mode is good for learning how the vehicles handle and the general controls, such as winching, switching vehicles and the like, and most maps can be finished in less than an hour.
Hardcore takes away teleporting vehicles back to garages, increases gas consumption and damage, and punishes you for driving with your differential lock engaged too fast.  This is more intense, I find it more enjoyable now that I know how the game works, but it easily increases how long a single session lasts.  Hour long maps for me have gone on for 3+ before I've had to ditch the game.
Even if you ignore doing the objectives and just horse around with some virtual offroading with friends, that's a blast too.  I could spend a good hour or so just running the jeep or one of the lighter utility trucks through the bush.
Well worth the time and Oovee seems to update it fairly cosistently with good size updates.

I'm a big Fallout fan and this game seemed to be just my thing. You can manage a Vault as Overseer build resource rooms and assign the right vault dwellers according to their SPECIAL stats to it which alsop raises their happiness which is a really nice way of managing.
PRO:
You can even build scavanger teams that do missions in the Wasteland which brings XP to them and loot for you and the Vault.
There are also mini challenges which bring you additional goodies.
This game uses different kind of currencies:
* There are caps which are needed to build rooms and buy other stuff
* There is real time which is needed for different actions to take place. The time ranges from mere seconds to full hours depending on the action. Good thing is you can log out and the time counts down as well.
* There is Nuka Cola Quantum which let's you skip the time requirements some actions have. You can buy NCQ using real money or find it in the world. I think it's mostly optional to use them.
You can equip your Vault dwellers with new clothes/armor which increase their SPECIAL Values.
You can equip your Vault dwellers with guns which increase their attack values once they have to fight.
There are events that trigger when your Vault dwellers have to fight.
If a Vault Dweller dies you can revive him using caps.
CONTRA:

Oh boy where to start ?
to be perfectly honest this game's a bundle of bad game design, frustration and lazyness that very nearly prevented more EDF games to be released to the west.
for thoses of you hesitating between EDF:IA and EDF 4.1
DO NOT get Insect armageddon
Its the single worst EDF game out there and you'll get fed up very quickly of the bullsh*t this is gonna put you through
so let me explain WHY its a bad game
First up: Aesthetics
This game is part of that era of gaming where game devellopers had either all gone colorblind or were in severe depression.
What you'll get here is a bunch generic space marines just barely hiding the fact they're trying to pull the whole "gears of war" non-sense of "little colors, ugly fridges for character" angle, wich move like they've got something stuck in their *ss and reload their guns by stroking it and reaching for lube in between each stroke leading to very delayed results (more on that later), save for a single class wich instead of stroking his shaking his gun arm like he's trying to shake the gun loose instead of reloading it, but at the very least it won't look as aggravating as the former, speaking of guns, each class has ONE model for each gun type and doesn't change dependant on the gun so if you're hoping for good-looking weapons, I've some bad news for you....
Characters aren't the only thing that are lackluster as the game seems to pride itself in the fact all buildings (save for thoses outside the map, more on that later) however the devellopers seem to have very quickly grown shy about that and hid the whole thing behind grey blobs of particle effects wich more often than not last far too long for what they do, not to mention most buildings you'll find here are copy-pasted building wich are crammed together as densely as possible to make extra sure you can't see sh*t when they inevitably get destroyed
as far as ennemies go they all more or less look like rubber toys of some kind wich either move in the most generic fashion possible
Now onto gameplay:
What you're looking at here, is the laziest attempt at a third person shooter I've seen yet, and GOD KNOWS I'm not picky,
the main gameplay loop you'll experience is as follows
Choose class, choose guns (or "buy" basic ones with a slow accumulating money thats earned through score)
go into mission
shoot things till dead
go to next place
shoot again
go to next place
shoot again
hold "use" on something for a couple of seconds (bear in mind if something touches while holding use, the progress on holding use starts over from scratch)
go to next place
and so on so forth...
Now that wouldn't be bad if the "shooting things" part wasn't as boring as watch grass grow, unfortunately you won't have fun chances are, since you have access to a total of 6 types of weapons, three of wich are useful (as in required to use "useful") and 3 are pointless as you'll literally never have a opportunity to use them to full potential.
Assuming you use the "useful" weapons you'll still have to deal with a design "faux pas" that made me hate Gears of war (wich I'll refer to as GoW for short) with a passion, wich is the active reload system, everytime you reload a gun you get a timing mini-game to reload faster, and unlike GoW, nothing else, again if you like this kind of thing it wouldn't be so bad except for a LOT OF PROBLEMS WITH THAT IDEA.
1: Unlike GoW, you have no point during you're in "cover" or safe, the game more or less plays like Serious sam where most of your time spent is spent going one direction and firing in the opposite, so having to deal with that crap on top ain't exactly helping
2: The way weapons work in this game is that each "weapon" has its own reload timer (during wich the reload animation just keeps looping non-stop till its finished) and the way it works with the reloading game is that fast reloading weapons are easier to reload and slow reloading are harder to reload, wich is the most backwards crap I ever saw, if slow weapons had a easier reload it would help them keep up with faster reload weapons and give you an actual reason to use that one gun that takes 5 seconds of stroking instead of that other gun wich takes 2 seconds (wich can be further reduced to 1 second easily) almost anytime because you're almost guaranteed to out damage the slower gun
Speaking of damage, there is no "strategy" in this game, its just a raw damage race to whoever deals more damage as your pathetic mobility won't help you dodge 9 times out of 10, in fact the most likely way you'll die is by damaging yourself with your own gun
Speaking of health and guns, each class has a "EXP bar" wich fills using score from the missions you complete, until you "level up" your stats will sit there doing nothing, so if you find a mission too difficult, all you can do is find a mission and spam the hell out of it till you actually level up and gain access to guns wich aren't quite as pathetic, and do I have some bad news for you if you hate grinding.
first up the AI squad mates the game gives you will siphon away score by killing mobs, making your accumulation of score even slower on top of them being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that can make your explosive weapons go off in your face point blank, have them try to shoot "through" you and subsequently deal you damage, perhaps even stunning you if the bot attempts using a explosive weapon of his own....on top of that the option to disable them must be UNLOCKED by completing a, thankfully, pathetically short campaign of 15 levels (for comparison EDF 4.1 has a minimum of 89)
secondly the amount of score asked per level up is far too high to make the game enjoyable as if you ARE grinding to make it less of a chore, peoples say that playing dark souls games is "like bashing your head against a wall until the wall breaks" and I say NAY, THIS is bashing your head against a wall INDEED, its slow, painful, frustrating and after you're done you get to see YET ANOTHER wall you need to bash and that one's even bigger...
and the "difficulty" levels of the game wich are supposedly what gives it more replayability does litterally nothing but multiply all the stats of the mobs by 3, thats it, no new ennemies, no new attacks, no new weapons, no new vehicles (long story short about thoses, they have more health move slower and do less damage than your character and out of 6 vehicles 4 of them are turrets and arguably the mech is a turret with legs)
at the end of the day, the game feels like a unity asset flip: ugly, lazy and boring as sin

this is a cute little game that combines real-time-strategy with a great story and many other goodies. it has great visuals and art design which is adorned with good music. the game world is really interesting and will captivate you with its alien atmosphere. story is also good, but the game needs more lore to fill this beautiful alien world. base building is very minimalistic. while, this might be good a thing for some people, it's not my cup of tea. more and varied buildings would be a very nice addition. units, on the other hand, are much more varied, but a few more distinct units would certainly add a bit a little bit more color to the game. units can be customized by equipping them with item that drop from the enemies or chests. they can also be given permanent mutations. this mutations are purchased with the dna currency that is gained by scrapping items. the combat in the game feels a bit simplistic. it is there and it works, but don't expect much. puzzles can get a bit problematic if you forget paying attention to your missions. overall, for all its shortcomings this is still a good game that stands out as a unique piece in the genre, i've really enjoyed playing it and would recommend it if you like strategy games and a good story.

Templar Battleforce is a great game made by amazing devs. It is a squad based, tactical combat RPG centered on your very own squad of Templar Knights. Your Knights are part of the last Templars in the new Quadrant, charged with protecting the new home of the Star Traders Union from hostile threats, from the Xeno menace to hidden traitors and Rogue Star Traders.
The game allows a large amount of tactical flexibility, letting any combination of Templars classes succeed with the right tactics and squad advancement. Individual Knights are highly customizable, from their physical and mental qualities, to their training and deployment, each Templar is a valuable asset on the battlefield. Buffs and special ablities are limited, as are the supplies used to deploy Templars and their battlefield Ordnance, adding another layer to the strategy offered by this game.
Combined with the Requestion tree and branching missions, Templar Batttleforce is a great game where every playthrough can be approached differently and still be successful. Don't be mistaken, that success requires strategy, skill, and luck, and victory can and will be costly if you are not careful.

Overall, this game is pretty good. The gameplay, albeit a little difficult at times, will never cease to entertain you. It is one of my favourite indie games.
That being said, it is still an indie game, and didn't have the manpower to make everything perfect: Namely, the graphics, music, and story line. The story line isn't bad, per say, but it is clear it was written by a single person with a lot of other things to do, so many plot holes and nonsensical elements exist. A similar story goes with the graphics-- they aren't bad or anything, (and are pretty decent for an indie game) but indie game devs just can't compete with the army of graphics designers large game companies have at their disposal. The music, on the other hand, is a different story. I highly recommend muting it. It is extremely repetitive and a bit distracting.
In spite of these things, I still recommend this game. They do not interfere too much with the game itself at all, and the game itself is pretty awesome. Just mute the music, will ya?

This has got to be one of the most boring and most disjointed games I have never had the pleasure to play.
This game has recently had a name change, for the second time, because for some reason these developers change the ♥♥♥♥ing name of their game whenever they release a "big update". This game was and still is a buggy pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥since launch and despite these "big updates" the bugs remain. First time they changed the name, they didn't fix anything... They just added a microtransaction store. Because they changed the name it caused a lot of bugs with Steam and it brought the game back on the front page of the Steam store and it did NOT deserve it. And now they did the same♥♥♥♥♥♥but it didn't seem to break the Steam Store like last time; No, all this update added was some hats, controller support (which by the way made it so that it only shows the Xbox controller buttons in the main menu, well done guys), and some game modes. I didn't even bother to play any of the other game modes after seeing how godawful their MAIN gamemode is.
So what actually is Orion Dino Beatdown/Horde/Prelude you ask? Well, it's a horde mode game involving dinosaurs. A fairly simple concept: there are waves, there are enemies, you kill enemies, progress through the waves and so it goes on. But the presentation and gameplay are so horrible that it doesn't work right (which is probably why they added the other game modes to make up for the garbage that they have created).
Presentation: This game looks hideous, even for an Unreal Engine 3 game, and it runs terribly dispite how bad it looks. I had to lower all the settings down to get a decent framerate and the game definitely does not look good enough to justify it. And it appears that they added a disgusting cell shaded look that just seems completely out of place recently, weird black outlines on some places. Besides graphics, the animations are atrocious and the modeling on the guns look pathetic, the sound design is just bad, many of the guns feel weak as a result of having poor animations and sound quality. ♥♥♥♥ing magnums should not sound like BB guns. The dinosaurs look alright, decent enough modeling and sound design... Until they attack you with their adorable little nibbling animations, making them look completely unthreatening. Yeah, this game doesn't look good at all.
But ok, graphics aren't important, gameplay is what matters in a game, right? Of course, only one problem, THIS GAME IS HORRIBLE! The gameplay is so bland and generic, it has nothing original about it, it only takes game mechanics from other games, and the mechanics that it takes it doesn't do as well as where they were originally taken from. I mentioned before how the guns feel weak, and they really do. Nothing has any of the OOMPH you would otherwise see in  a competent FPS. This game's gunplay is almost as bad as Borderlands', and the guns themselves are completely uninteresting. There's very little variety in the enemies and it gets boring to fight the same dinosaurs REALLY FAST. So the gameplay is also a failure here.
So it looks bad, sounds bad and plays bad. Is there any point in getting this game? Absolutely not. It's not even so bad that it's funny, it's just awful, it isn't even worth the $1. If you want to play a good horde mode game, I highly suggest Killing Floor, it does everything right where Orion does wrong. I decided to write this review now because it seems like the developers are trying to squeeze out every little bit that they can from this game and it's just depressing to see. It feels like they really tried their best here but this just doesn't work. Guys, this game is not good, you have to move on, from here you have two choices: You either realise that game development isn't your thing, or you improve upon what you did here and take note of your mistakes. Either way, let go of this game and focus on stuff you really want to do, rather than just change the game's name multiple times and milk the ever living♥♥♥♥♥♥out of it.

I love this game, to put it bluntly. I got it while it was on sale for $3.74, and I got just over 17 hours of fantastic, captivating gameplay out of it. The art style is quirky, and like a hybrid between comics, and cartoons. The soundtrack is great, and always engaging. VO's are done beautifully, though the lines at time could use some work. There's some obvious flaws with the game, such as a few of the typical clichés, and the cutscenes look worse than in game dialogue. Speaking of igd, it's done in a very cool manner here, where the background fades out a bit, and you see very high res, animated images of the speaking character that's quite engaging. The concept is quite cool, and though not original, is also not overdone. Combat is fluid when you get the hang of it, and I found it quite easy to go flying across a level, killing everyone in my path. The controls are solid, and responsive, and the game is not too difficult, even on the highest difficulty. Finding all 12 caged friends was a challenege, that kept me playing, just so I could see a 100% completion on my save file.
Overall, a 9.5/10. My only gripes, are the weird degredation in graphics for the cutscenes, and the often cheesy, and clichéd dialogue. Definitely worth a buy

Should you buy this game?
The answer is YES if any of the following apply:
1. You like rhythm games. Nothing is more satisfying for a rhythm gamer than a game that is dynamic, and not just about memorizing. You have to react to what the games throws at you.
2. You like dungeon crawler games. This is one of the best games when it comes to replay value, in my opinion. There are so many different things to try. I played over 30 hours in alpha/beta, and I am definitely going to spend another 20+ just trying out new builds on my character or creating new dungeon maps.
3. You like skill based games. Seriously, this game takes some skill to master. So many different situations to overcome. There are even multiple characters and modes to play in to make it even more of a challenge!
My experience:
I played this game in early access, and it was an absolute blast of a game! Updates were frequent and so much quality content was being added. The rhythm mechanics are great, the different weapons make it fun to play over and over, and the boss fights are sublime.
About 6 months ago, I stopped playing because I didn't have time anymore.
I just came back today after the main update, and wow, I have some things to say. This game is even better than I could have possibly thought. I don't normally write reviews twice on games, but I'll make an exception for COTND. I just started to stratch the surface of the new characters, items, and bosses. So far, I am LOVING it. I don't feel overwhelmed by new content at all, in fact I am enjoying discovering new items and enemies. The story mode is just what the game needed--something to tie together the characters, bosses, and theme of the game. I can't wait to play this a ton over the summer!
While I haven't beaten this yet on steam, I did play it to the end on my phone and loved it. Heard a sequel was coming out and I got right back in the groove on my computer.

10,000,000. An odd name for a game, yes. But it is also the purpose of the game. To reach 10,000,000 points and escape the dungeon is your ultimate goal. So is the run worth it, or should you just pass this one up and find a new number to satisfy you? Let’s find out.
This one will be short and sweet, like the game itself turns out to be. Well, maybe not so sweet as it does tend to end with you dying. Quite a lot in fact. The gameplay is the tried and true match-3 formula we all know and love. With some minor combat elements tossed in, of course. Match three or more swords or staves and you will do damage to your enemies. Beat them and you continue along your merry way and earn more points. Along the way, you will collect gold and various resources, which can be used to upgrade your weapons, magic, and armor. Upgrading these will in turn allow you to get further in your run, collect more gold, upgrade more, and so on. The end goal is to reach 10,000,000 points and earn your freedom.
If you’re a fan of addictive match-3 games and enjoy some RPG-lite gameplay, you won’t go wrong with this one. The game clocks in at around 5-10 hours, and is well worth the small price tag.

Always a game to be had and weekly updates.  This is one of my games that any time day or night I can go to and find a game.  While it can be frustrating to learn the community is usually pretty helpful to newbies, particularly if you play on the rookie/rookie friendly servers.  The learning curb is a little steep but this is greatly helped by in game viewable tuturials.  I highly suggest you watch videos on how to command in youtube seperately though before you consider trying to command youself.  And when you do in general it's best that you wait until a time when no one else wants to command and then you can pipe up on mic that you'd like to give it a shot that you've done your homework.  It's usually best if you wait until you lose your rookie status which takes awhile unless you are putting some serious playtime in.
The two teams couldn't be more different both to command and to play, which really lends to the emmersion.  Although if you have a choice you're probably better off playing as marines especially if you haven't checked out the tuturial videos which I highly recommend especially playing as one of the various alient types.  There is a very active workshop community which you can make use of to get various helpful mods or cosmetic ones if you want to spice things up for yourself.   This is well worth the price of admission as the game shows no signs of going dead anytime soon.
If I were to complain about anything it would be that the balance sometimes favors one side or another but as I said they come out with updates every week so if something is noticed as being too OP they will usually fix it.  My only other gripe is that sometimes I log in and there are 3-7 servers going that I usually like to play on and they are all full so I might have to spend 15-30 minutes in a low popped server until it builds up into a proper game.  Most servers are full at 18-22 give or take a few, but there are a few servers that use enlargened maps with max players set to 50 or more, although those only really get popped during peak hours usually.
The action can be quite intense even in pub games and it's not uncommon for people to get excited, if anyone ever gives you any grief just say your new and if you don't know what you did wrong ask what you could have done better.  Almost everyone uses their Mic btw, especially if they are commanding.

Disclaimer:  The game itself is not inherently bad.  I did put over 15 hours into it before uninstalling it.  You've got the mechanics of Bloons TD 5 coupled with a competitive multiplayer aspect.  However, there are many flaws within the game's mechanics that simply make it such that I would not tell my friends about it.
First, the game is straight up Pay2win.  Bloons td5 is good, this is a cash grab.  The game would be better balanced if they just charged five bucks for it and put everyone on equal footing, but that's not the case.  You buy tower unlocks, which give you an advantage over your opponent.  You buy energy, which gives you an advantage over your opponent.  You buy club access (unobtainable by non-paying), which gives you access to more arenas with special rules.
Second, there's some balance issues.  Did you spend $10 on the newbie starter pack?  If you did, you have enough medallions to buy the COBRA tower.  This tower makes it impossible to lose versus players that don't have this tower.  In defense mode, you gain extra lives every fifteen seconds, which is sizable.  In assault mode, your opponent loses 2 of their 150 lives every fifteen seconds, PER COBRA TOWER you have.  That is to say, you will win versus your opponents without having to watch a single bloon go by them.  Buy these towers and upgrade them, then wait 'em out.  In both assault and defense modes (both of the f2p modes), this tower also increases your cash income by giving you extra money every round.
--If you have it, where's the fun in stomping people that don't have it?
--If you don't have it, where's the fun in losing a game where the rules don't matter?
Third, the meta is very stale.  At the higher ranks, everyone uses the same tower loadout.  Just google "bloons td battles chipper farm".
-Did you NOT spend $10 on this, because the game is supposedly free?  Many of your matches will be fair, but if you see a COBRA tower on the other side, just surrender, because you're losing this round.  Not to the rules of the game, but rather, to Teh UlTiMaTe ToWeR!!11!!one!!!
-Your energy replenishes at a rate of 5 per hour, to a max of 20.  Is that too slow?  Buy more energy with real monies!  Is the energy cap too low?  Buy an increase!  Energy has a tangible effect on the game, most notably, by increasing the attack speed of all your towers for a short time (a la the MIB Call to Arms effect in Bloons TD 5).  Are you out of energy and refuse to spend cash on the game?  Your opponents may simply have an advantage over you, as they can use this ability and you cannot.
-Instead of using towers to unlock higher tiers, you use medallions to unlock higher tiers as your level increases.  Don't feel like using medallions and/or waiting for your level to get high enough?  Guess what!  Five bucks gets around all that noise!
-Card mode is akin to Hearthstone, in that "whoever has the most sunk into it wins".  The details and mechanics are too esoteric to go into here, but it's even worse than the assault/defense mode balances.
-To top it all off, the game is full of cheaters.  Just google "bloons TD battles hacks" and click on any of the myriad results to get an example of this.
TL, DR:   The game would be better if the following occurred.
-Strict and immediate punishment for cheaters.
-COBRA towers removed or rebalanced. (Pay money to get these!)
-An equal amount of energy given to both players at the start of a match. (Pay money to have more!)
-Tower level limits equal on both players in a match. (Pay money to max towers!)

Oh boy...this ♥♥♥♥ing game...well, wrote a Review for EDF4.1, may as well do it here too.
In said previous review of Earth Defense Force 4.1, Shadow of New Despair...I said this game was like an American Made Mutation of a fantastic Japanese Series. Kind of like how we tried to make our own "Godzilla" of some kind but called it "Zilla" instead, and it apperently sucked. Hard. (Thankfully the original creators bought his Licenseing out, comepletely remade his bio and such, and proceeded to absolutely murder him in the first movie he came in. Or at least that's what I heard.)
This game, thankfully, is not EXACTLY like Zilla. It wasn't terrible but...it's still a sort of Black Sheep of the franchise for a good reason. It tries it's best to stay close to the formula of the classic games...but it feels as if it's tried to downgrade most, if not all, of the aspects they tried to stick to.
For instance: This game is friggen SHORT. Only around 15 or so different missions for the campaign plus a few Survival Missions which take place in the exact same maps, which is NOTHING compaired to even the Very First EDF Game on the Playstation. To compare, 4.1 has 89 missions in the Solo Campaign, 9 Bonus Missions in the the Multiplayer to make it 98 there, 23 or so missions in the first DLC Pack for the game, and 20+ in the second pack. That's close to TWO HUNDRED INDIVIDUAL MISSIONS to do!
Next, it's difficulty. This game only has three to choose from...yeah. JUST THREE. Normal, Hard, and Inferno. Compaired to the norm of EDF, which is FIVE, this is yet ANOTHER downgrade because it makes the game way...WAY less accessable. Say you're a New Player to the game, and you start on Normal. If ya find yourself being a bit challenged on there, say it's actually the first Shooter that you as a Player have gotten into and don't know how to properly play, you could go to Easy and ease yourself a bit slower into it, and work your way to the harder difficulties. That is nowhere near the case here.
Another thing I should mention is how the player grows stronger here. In the other games, only your Equipment grows stronger as you collect bits and pieces to up your Arsenal and Armor. Everything else? Depends on YOUR skill. Depends on YOUR Talent. Your reactions, your planning, your aim, everything. It's mostly on YOU to get you through the fights. It's all on your own Experience.
Not here. This game goes for a pretty damn basic method of getting you stronger for the fights ahead. You can collect some weapons out in the field when you defeat certain enemies, sure...but for the most part? You're grinding Mission after Mission not to collect gear...but to get more Currency and Experience POINTS. These, respectively, allow you to buy your character more gear, and Level You Up increase your HP Ammount and the weapons available to purchase. To me, this system isn't as Immersive, as Creative, or as FUN as the other games.
Speaking of Fun, my next topic is just that. The fact that this game isn't as Fun as the actual EDF Series. Hell, some people (me included) could find this game...kinda boring really. Besides JUST having 15 missions, they don't really even seem to feel any different at all.
The Classic EDF Games hold some kind of Magic that keeps every single mission feeling fresh and fun to fight through. It's all fairly Colorful and Vibrant, you can Explore every inch of the map you're given in each mission within it's MASSIVE boundaries, Explosions feel Inherently Satisfying, Bug and Robot corpses litter the battlefield after exploding into Blood or...well just flat out explode to let you see how much you've accomplished...and it all just douses you in Internal Happiness that you simply can't stop,
This game? Is almost the complete opposite. Everything is put into more "realistic" boring brown filters, Explosions feel like you're shooting Weak♥♥♥♥♥Firecrackers at the Enemy (Classic EDF had BETTER Firecrackers as an ACTUAL WEAPON), The maps are far more linear due to stupid plot reasons (i'll get back to this in a second), the Enemy Corpses disappear as soon as they die, and it's all just so slow and sluggish...it's like you're going through a Daily Slog each and every time you come across a horde of enemies. That's terrible, really.
But it gets worse when I move on to My Last and MOST CERTAINLY Least favored aspect of this game: It's story. Oh god, it's story is just...no. THIS aspect is just flat-out ruined, and is the worst part about the game bar-none. Classic EDF had Rediculous Basic. "Giant Insects and Massive Machines have come to destroy everything we love and hold dear! Here, take this FORT KNOX LEVEL OF GUNS stuffed in your locker, fellow EDF Soldiers with their own funny Dialogue who will dance and Sing with you on command, and an EXTREME amount of PURE HYPE, and go save our world!"
This game? STUPID Basic. "Our mission is to save the world from the threat of Large Bugs and Accompanying Machines. Here is a truck filled with a large arsenal that you can use. You will have two Squad Mates who will follow and assist you in combat, but you can't interact with them even though they have randomized voice lines that aren't interesting. Follow our waypoints, stick to your objectives, follow this linear path because the Ravagers have created Barriers that we can't cross through-" Ugh, okay yeah. I can't even continue with that...i've made MYSELF uninterested.
The worst part is? They actually tried (and failed miserably) to make it a little bit more serious. The Highest Points of it, which really isn't saying much, goes as follows. They build up this mysterious "Cube", only for them to say later that it's basically just a really powerful bomb. They activate said Cube to completely destroy a Giant Insect-...oh sorry, they also call THOSE Ravagers here for some stupid reason. They activate it to destroy a RAVAGER Nest, only for their escape chopper to crash and burn, and command says that your team will be "acceptable losses". Oh, and the Mothership just appears from out of nowhere at the Final Mission.
{Spoilers Ahead}
With all that being said however...i'm sure there are some people out there who may enjoy this format of game. There is a Philosophy across this world that, if you search long and hard enough: There IS a game out there that can possibly suit you. This one could very well be yours if you take a look at it yourself.
For me however, it was a no-go. My final rating is a 4/10 with a No Recommendation.

First of all, this game shows a lot of promise. In one hour I was able to complete the first mission (the tutorial?) and quite enjoyed the RPG and RTS aspects this game employs. The atmosphere is quite unique, with the game largely taking place in beautifully detailed subterranean caverns on an alien world. The water effects are rendered quite well, and the graphics are definitely impressive for an indie developer's foray into Steam early access games.
The goal of the game is quite simple: build a hive to support your alien insects and produce units (or defensive turrets) to destroy the hostile creatures that litter the in game world. You must support your hive by producing workers that can supply food, minerals, and produce buildings using in game resources. Although the first level is understandably quite easy, I have heard that the other missions are quite challenging. As of this review, there are five missions in total.
Understandably, as this is an early access game, there are a few bugs but nothing game breaking. When fighting enemy units, for example, sometimes only half of the enemy group will engage your army. The game also lacks some staple RTS features, like multiplayer or custom games. Once this game is released I'm sure more features will be added, so this is nothing major. I look forward to completing the remaining missions.

Dust is a side-scrolling beat-em-up/platformer with rpg elements in the form of equipment upgrades and a basic stat buy leveling system. It is also an excellent game.
The plot is fairly straightforward, at least from the outset. You are Dust, a young man who has lost his memories. Dust has found himself caught in a dangerous situation of which he is clearly a part, but has no idea how or why.
The story is simple, but perfectly fine within the scope of the game. It is backed up by mostly beautiful graphics (the character frames leave something to be desired), fairly good voice acting, and acceptable music.
The mechanics work well with the game. In my gaming career, this has been the best game I've played in terms of control options. It is equally playable on control pad, keyboard and mouse, or pure keyboard. Combat is simple but smooth, the menus are easy to understand, and the platforming puzzles show very little repetition.
I highly recommend this game for anyone who likes action platformers, unless you absolutely can't stand furries.

Dust: An Elysian Tail is part of a well-known genre of side-scrolling action/adventure games. In many ways, the story is unoriginal, the characters are obvious archetypes, and the dialogue is corny, but that did not make me enjoy the game any less. The clichés aside, this is a game that has a very solid art style, a no-frills plot, and a beautifully-simple fighting mechanics and inventory systems. This game takes themes we are all very famliar with and polishes them up into a fun adventure that is engaging and memorable. The road this game travels is well-trodden, and the developers are very well aware of this which they pay homage to in many homages and references to other popular games. The characters frequently break the fourth wall and I felt that gave the game more endearing qualities than if it took itself too seriously.
Nothing ground breaking here, but if you are looking for a fun, straight-forward, well-assembled game, give Dust a try!

This game was amazing with a TRULY GREAT STORY. 92/100. Absolute definitely replayability with two major story arcs and many minor ones.
It is Skyrim-like with action-RPG elements, but it is definitely not a true open-world game like Skyrim or The Witcher 3. The graphics are astonishing. If you have the card to handle it (r9 290/290x or 780/780ti) you will want to max it out AND edit the .ini file to increase view distances. Pop-in was not present at all when I did this, and distant objects were crisp and lush.

I bought this game because I really much like the art style, and I am fascinated with Japanese culture along with stealth games. I am fairly new to the stealth-game genre, having played the new Theif and Dishonored. This runs along the same lines with three ranks you can obtain that goes by killing all enemies, remaining undetected, and killing no one and a score along with it, much like Devil May Cry as well which handed out a score based on actions and so forth.
In this game, the pace is much more casual and you need patience or good timing if you want to go quickly. I loved it...until chapter 8 of 13 when I encountered a sub-boss. 20 deaths later I called it quits so I don't come to hate the game. I admit I messed up on leveling up my skills and it screwed me over for the harder fights, so I will have to start over. What I find is a major issue is the autosave feature and that it's not broken up periodically, so in a big area you spent 20 minutes meticulously planning and timing to avoid killing anyone, Boom, you die and you restart ALL the way back to the beginning. I found myself trying to force an autosave by spending skill points or refilling my skills at a shrine, but doesn't exactly work out. I really wish there was a manual save so I don't have to kill everyone just to complete the same area I have been trying to complete for an hour.
So, yeah, hate the autosave-only part of this game and the first sub-boss, but more so for how it's set up.
Adding this is after the fact. Tried to start a new game and was unable. You get two options: Continue and Story. Story just continues you with the mainly storyline. -_-  So yeah I cannot start a new game...may have to try and delete files...

I bought this game about 3 days ago and I've already got about 19hrs on record. However, that's only because the intro is genuinely interesting and remains interesting for the first hour or so of the game. However, when a certain act of betrayal happens and the storyline properly begins, it quickly becomes slightly less exciting. The storyline following this incident is your classic tail of retribution and revenge, which is understandable when put into context, yet still manages to seem unimaginative and just like any other game that features treachery (GTA:SA, for example).
In short, it ends up as a constant repetative loop of shooting warehouses up. Twice over. Yep, you shoot some place up to provoke a top gangsta then go back and talk to one of your associates across the other side of town, only to be told in a short conversation that they've heard that the gangsta you've just tried to provoke out of hiding has just conveniently arrived at the warehouse you've just turned into a blood bath. Then, you're tasked with driving all the way back to said building so that you can talk (or slaughter) the mob boss, once again shooting your way through the new gangsta npc's that occupy the warehouse, as you step over the bodies of the ones you executed and slaughtered just 10 minutes beforehand. Naturally, this makes for irritatingly repetative gameplay after a while, considering that you literally have to shoot your way through the same place twice - only taking a break half way through to speed across town and back.
Lastly, the shooting and combat system is pretty much the same as the rebooted version of Tomb Raider, just without the archery. The game often feels like Driver: San Fransisco, particularly with the quality detail on the cars, yet devestatingly poor handling that features in both games. There's a massive city, with quality detailing in the references to 1960's culture - particularly the reoccuring racism and discrimination in addition to the white-male societal dominance. Such a shame that there's not-one-thing to do that will entice you to explore the city. There's nothing social at all. You can't go get something to eat or drink, you can't play any ingame minigames, gambling is illegal so there's none of that, you can't get a hair cut, buy new clothes, or anything else like that. It's all "go pick up contraband for one of your (many) clients" or "go 'have a discussion' (which means shoot some ♥♥♥♥♥es up) with this senior mob person".
I know I've told you everything that the game lacks, but the truth is that it starts off good and goes down hill gradually from there. I'm only half way through and I'm hoping something exciting will happen soon to keep me engaged. I genuinely doubt that there will be a reason to keep playing after the main storyline is finished, because all it will be then is a 1960's gangsta boss simulator, where you have to do favours for your clients (who should be doing the ♥♥♥♥ing job themselves) just to keep them "loyal" (according to the game), meaning that you have to keep them interested despite being their boss.
Despite all this, I still recommend the game. I didn't at first, but you can't overlook the quality in the other aspects of emmersion and atmosphere that has clearly went into making a realistic society and environment that does not shy away from the abhorant discrimination and political incorrectness of its set era. The soundtrack, whilst only featuring a humble collection of about 3-4 radio stations, still features what most of us would call a 'fire playlist'. Originals by Patsy Cline, The Rolling Stones, Beach Boys, Aretha Franklin, Elvis, Johnny Cash, Marvin Gaye, Supremes, The Miracles and that's just a fraction! A lot of these are already on my playlist so I was made up when I heard them playing for the first time.
You can upgrade your cars in mod-shops like those in GTA. You also have distinctively similar upgrades for your weapons and even you as the protagonist (such as health improvements) to the interface seen in the rebooted games of the Tomb Raider series. It definitely has room for imrpovement, but it's still a relatively great game in it's own right.

For reference, I just beat the campaign for the first time (I played in normal). I usually like turn by turn strategy and tactical games like civilization, fire emblem, shining force, ...
Templar Batteleforce is a tactical rpg type game which is mostly a sequence of fights with team building in between fights; in the same way your typical fire emblem would be.
It took me about 40 hours to beat the game for the first time which makes the game an appropriate length in my opinion. It is about 40-ish battles. The game features many difficulty level and probably has a reasonnable replay value. I plan on at least playing the full game a second time, and probably more to explore different team builds.
What really did the game for me is how battles are constructed. Essentially the better you "score" in a battle, the more experience and RP (essentially money) you get out of the battle. The score is essentially computed depending on how fast you accomplished the objectives, how many ennemie you killed and how many secondary objective (often unknown to you in advance) you accomplished. This gives a sense of urgency in the battles, encourages you to explore, but exploring is dangerous.
An interesting mechanic in the game is the concept of "heat points". Essentially all movement and action a character does makes its suit heat. And when overheated, he starts taking damage, losing ability to perform some types of action, or completely shut down. It is something that usually does not come in the way too much, but it is also something that you can not ignore.
The team build part of the game is interesting. Essentially the number of "points" you can allocate to characters really mean that you can not max-out a character. You have to make hard choices. For instance, you pretty much have to choose between a scout that can scan large portion of the maps and move fast, and a scout that deals massive damage at a distance; you can try a middle ground but it might not be best. Similarly with the engineer, either you get a tact point expert to help take and control tactical points (which are supply point on the map), or you make a battle engineer which buffs your units and is reasonnably useful in a fight. Doing both is a possible but serious compromise,
One of the problem I have with the team building is that the UI is a bit awkward and it took me almost an entire run through the game before I had a clear enough understanding of the game mechanics to optimize my team carefully. There are a few dimensions to the game system (roll to hit, damage reduction, peircing damage ignore part of the armor, bio-damage do damage in the long run, ...) which are all pretty much independent in the character sheet. It is sometimes hard to see how much point to spend in one aspect. Fortunately, you can "respec" your units from scratch between battles, so if you misunderstood the impact of a game mechanic, you can correct your team building mistakes for the next battle.
In term of difficulty, there are many difficulty levels. I play a lot of tactical games and normal was too easy for me. If you are used to that kind of games, push it one notch up. Though, it seems that at higher level, there is perma death, so... be careful.
I really liked some of the options in the game. Soldiers can use "overwatch" to cover some squares of the map and shoot enemie entering the zone. hydras can use napalm to set some squares of the map on fire causing damage to units passing through. Engineers can build turrets to defend some parts of the map. So overall, I feel like as a player, your decision can shape how the skirmish unfols.
One thing that could be annoying is that the ennemies can pop out of many places with no way for you to know in advance, and they usually play in the turn they appear. So you can get in situation where a unit pops out and deals you damage without much you could have done. (overwatch can be useful there.)
I find that the units you control have a very limitted field of vision. And sometimes, this can be very annoying.
Something good is that the game developpers are quite responsive. I don't know how long they will be maintaining the game. But for now, they reply on the forum almost immediately. I pointed out a bug that was essentially fixed in a day. They take suggestion.
The storyline is pretty much irrelevant. I do not feel like you have a clear control of the story nor a clear idea of the lore of the game. It is a fairly straight forward story, with a bit of details if you want to know more. Clearly the story is not the focus of the game. Overall, I feel like it is appropriate for this type of game.
The graphics are alright. It is a seen from atop game. Nothing fancy, but it works. The graphic style is nice and enjoyable. I appreciated the fact that the style is overall coherent, many smaller games tend to have incoherency in style. But this one is profesionnal.
In term of sounds, the sfx are appropriate, but the background music sucks. The music is really subpar in this game. One of the track is pretty much a mix of a 8-second track with a 16-second track. The others are not much better. It drove my wife crazy. Fortunately, you can shut the music off and leave the sfx, and play your own music in the back. Makes the game much more enjoyable.
In summary, is this game perfect ? no. Is it the best tactical game out there? no. Is it fun and enjoyable? Yes. Is it worth its price? Absolutely.

Oh this is good. This game is real good. While lacking the polish of a finished title (still early access and all that) there is no doubt in my mind that The Hive is a game I'm glad I've had the opportunity to try out. The Hive is a RTS that is very heavy on the story elements. Basically, you'll be exploring this world as much as you will be smashing your foes and managing resources.
The story is your usual, "we had to escape Earth because it got screwed" storyline except instead of taking on the predictable role of the Human Race, you actually play as a mysterious Insectoid race known as The Hive. You'll solve puzzles while also killing animals for food and amassing hordes of insects to kill Lizardmen, skeletons and all manner of bad guys. You'll meet old gods, titan-like creatures and you'll have to bring down some seriously over powered enemies.
In terms of sound, artwork, and level design, this game exceeds on levels that very much remind me of Warcraft 3. Truly, the game actually feels very similar to WC3, except if you had a whole race devoted to large number horde tactics and passive buffs that make the horde even more powerful (Sort of like the beetle guys the undead had in FT). I love all the little details in this game as well. Like when your workers are harvesting resources, they create a little pile that actually gets bigger the more they gather and a tiny beetle creature comes and transports the resources back to the base. It's so insignificant but it's just an extra piece of world building that helps immerse one in the game. Mechanically, the game is just as sound, there are a few tactics that seem more effective than others and I'll refrain from spoiling anything for now but I'm sure as time goes on, it will be ironed out.
In summation, this game is pretty solid and I can't help but look optimistically towards it's final release.

The Hive is a RTS title, very representative of the genre. Like with similar games, you need to collect resources, build your base and gather enough troops to overcome the challenges of each level. What sets The Hive apart though, is the fact that is adding some really interesting RPG elements to the mix, elements that make this game a trully enjoyable experience.
As the leader of your insectoid race, you must complete the objectives that are given to you by your advisor and guide your race through the underworld of this alien world. Each level is beautiful and exotic and adds to the unique atmosphere of the game. As the story unfolds you also get info about the history of this world and the events that led to the current situation.
At the beginning the enemies are not very hard and quite passive, but as you unlock more maps they become stronger and more aggressive. Building your defenses fast will be necessary to survive. Once you learn how to deal with them, the game becomes easier. Boss fights are a whole other thing though. Bosses in The Hive have their own unique abilities and you need to follow a strategy to win against them. Just standing still, hitting them, waiting for their health to go down, wont work. This is why Boss fights in the game are so much fun.
By defeating enemies or simply by exploring the map you may get items as loot, items you can equip on your units and make them stronger, or dissolve and gain DNA. DNA is one of the resources in the game and you could say that it is the most important one. This is because with DNA you can unlock new skills and upgrade them or unlock new units, essential for your success. These two features make The Hive a great game. Also the fact that the skills you unlock and upgrade are permanent, make the experience a lot better.
Something i should mention is the lack of Fog of War on the levels. This means that the entire map is visible to the player and you can see when the enemies are preparing for an attack to your base. Although not a big deal for me, some might find this weird for a RTS title.
Overall, The Hive is a very enjoyable game worth taking a look at.

Aside from those issues it's a delight to play either alone or with friends. It controls and performs well, is easy to learn so you can jump into action, and has a pretty interesting neon-esque art style.
I highly recommend using a controller for this title, and note you can use the left analog stick to direct the ball's trajectory before you kick it (I didn't figure that out initially).
If you're looking for bursts of fun for maybe 5-15 minutes at a time I suggest you give Soccertron a go. Just take note that for the price you might only manage 1-3 hours of gameplay as that seems to be the medium, but if you or your friends enjoy it, I anticipate roughly 8-10 hours of game time in getting all achievements.

Not that this game seems to be in any desperate need of more positive reviews, but I had to put in my two cents. To tell a long story short, I think that Hotline Miami is a masterpiece of modern gaming.
The Pros:
Fantastic gameplay: Deaths are seemless into restarts as so not to be frustrating, the level design is fantastic, and the boss battles are memorable. Using every weapon feels great.
Crazy replayability: The main story isn't all that long, depending on how much you die, but there's a lot to do afterwards. The true ending requires going back to find all the secrets. If you want to 100% it like me, you have to get an A+ on every chapter, which is really hard, but so satisfying
Variability: Keeps the game fresh nicely. There are tons of weapons and guns, and over a dozen masks that can drastically change gameplay (or just add a filter, but still...)
Music: Has my second favorite soundtrack of all time- only second to Hotline Miami 2. The energetic, pounding house music fits perfectly with the gameplay and atmosphere.
Story: Hard to understand, but if you work for it, the story is really incredible. Most of the story is told through the enviroment, so you're left guessing on a lot of important information. The ambiguity is purpousful, and makes any glimmer of information you can find seem huge. HLM1 tells the how of the story, while HLM2 tells the why, but I think the combination of gameplay, sparse dialogue, and conflicting themes makes a much better story in HLM1.
Cons:
Uhhh? Sometimes the game doesn't register my finishers, which is annoying, but I can work with. The game crashes a little too often for my liking as well, but I can live with it.
All in all, I think this is an incredibly layered game. The gameplay, visuals, and sound are all great, but digging a little bit deeper can give you so much more. Many reviews would make HLM1 seem like a pointless slaughterfest, but there's a lot more than first meets the eye. I never thought I could become so attached to characters who hardly have any dialogue, if any at all. I might even go so far as to say the game has artistic qualities in how it uses ambiguity, enviroment, and gameplay to tell a compelling story. No steam library is complete without it.

So I've been playing this game for around 4 hours (at the time of writing this, I'll likely be playing for much longer), and I must say, this game rivals the Binding of Isaac in how creative and downright awesome it is. It even has music made by the very same guy, Danny Baranowski, all hail, who made the glorious soundtrack for the Binding of Isaac, Super Meat Boy, and many other games. The gameplay is smooth and flows very well. Crypt of the Necrodancer is just an all-around well designed game, and in my honest opinion it is well worth the $14.99 (or 24.99, if you bought the soundtrack, which you should also do.).

Short version: 7/10; only buy it at around $0.99 or a bundle, imo.
I didn't expect much from 10,000,000 coming in, but I was pleasantly surprised; I saw $0.99, and saw a game described as a puzzle / RPG, so I was sold. At the heart of the game is a "connect 3" game (I think that's the term...?); you have a board of tiles, and must match three or more to do something. While you're playing the game, you'll be faced with either enemies, a locked door, or a locked chest, and must match the correct corresponding tiles to advance. To combat the enemies, you must connect either the melee tiles (which can crit), or the magic tiles (which can have special effects, ranging from freezing them solid, to poisoning them). To combat the doors and/or chests, you must match the keys. Once you open the chest, you either get gold (one of three currencies used in the game to unlock / upgrade things), or a one-time use item that helps you in fighting. Other tiles that are used are: wood (currency), stone (currency), item (gives you an item to use in combat), and wildcard, which acts as anything, tile-wise.
There are a couple of things I don't like about the game, namely the fact that there are situations where it's virtually impossible to win. If the board gives you a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hand, you can't do anything about it (well, you can use an item to randomly change like, five of 25 tiles once...), and will lose. If you don't have any keys on the board, and you run into a chest, well, good luck. While I appreciate that the game has "stronger" and "weaker" monsters, they're not tuned very well; the dragons will make short work of you, unless you have items saved up for them specifically. The graphics might be a turn-off to some players. There's only one song, that's endlessly looped (didn't bother me, but I wanted to mention it). Another annoyance is that if you use your items early, before the enemy is properly aligned with you, you've wasted the item, and it does nothing. Really...? Finally, the hit-detection can be weird, since you *only* use the mouse for this game...most times it was okay, but I did notice it from time to time.
With all that said, I enjoy this type of game, and with light RPG elements, and the fact that certain tiles really only work with certain situations, I enjoyed the strategy... when I wasn't raging. As mentioned at the top, I would rate this a 7/10, but would only recommend it at around $1.00 or so (or if it's in a bundle).

Absolutely amazing. I never thought there would ever be a roguelike-rythm game, but here we are, and it's executed in such a way that this will probably end up being my favorite game of the year. The game is played using just arrow keys for movement and item usage, and it works really well.
The game appears as a standard roguelike dungeon crawler; you make tactical choices in turn-based style battles, find equipment and try to battle your way through dungeons. The difference is that the game focuses on forcing the player to keep in step with the beat of the song for movement and actions (traditionally what you'd consider to be "turns"), giving the player a bonus in gold which can be used to buy equipment if done without flaw. Failing to move with the beat will result in a missed action while all the enemies take a turn and losing this bonus.
I don't think I've ever played an RPG so easy to get into, yet challenging on many levels. It has a fun plot that works with the premise of the mechanics and the voice acting is actually very good. The music is superb, and if it's not your thing you can use your own music to power the gameplay.
I don't even think I have anything I could say needs improving. It supports controllers and even dance pads. There's a slightly less difficult mode meant specifically for playing with dance pads. They already have a character that doesn't need to move in time, turning the game into a traditional roguelike dungeon crawler if you want to get used to the game or want to take a break from the rythm aspects of the game. I mean, they thought of everything and the game is super polished, all that seems to be missing is four characters and the last zone (which I haven't even reached yet). This is seriously a game I wish I had helped made.

I have not played a game so well rounded and fun in such a long time.  I tried TF2 and a ton of random shooters and squad based games, but Paladins is seriously fun and has kept me wanting to play.  Even when it feels like you are losing, it's still super fun.  The champions have enough variety and different abilities to keep it interesting, nothing feels repetitive or "the same" between any of them.
You can create different builds using the card system to make your characters play way differently, and save your builds to load up depending on the map, team composition, and enemy composition.  For example, Ruckus (a front line tanky champion) can be built to have high mobility (normally he's relatively slow), or you can build him to be a super tank with sheilds that load quicker and cover more area etc.
Being able to plan loadouts for your champions is really great, (you create your loadouts outside of matches, so you can take the time to think them through).  The items you buy in the matches with points you earn from playing/killing are well balanced and allow further versatility for your champion.  (Heals too strong on enemy? Buy cauterize to reduce effectiveness of enemy heals when you shoot them).
It's still beta, but there are no serious issues.  At first, certain champions will seem impossible to counter (Fan favorites include Torvald, Evie, Ruckus) - but once you figure out their weaknesses you can feel the balance shifting as you get better at playing.  (Sure, Fernando has a huge sheild that people can stand behind, but he cant attack while using it - and your flankers can get behind him to snipe away anyone standing behind it)
The teamwork involved in winning really comes into the limelight when you reach competitive games (requires 12 champions at level 4 or higher to enter competitive) - And the limit of 2 in a party maximum to queue for competitive means you won't be fighting a 5 man premade uber-stomp group as a solo que.
If you want something that is honest fun, check this out.  You won't regret it.

A lot of things about The Hive are great, but being an early access game, there's obviously many things it is still lacking.
Positives:
-Great visuals, the evironment genuinely feels alive and alien and suits the gameplay well
-Great music, very tribal and gives you a sense that you're in a primordial ecosystem
-Fun as hell, I love controlling the units and getting them to attack/harvest/mine things
-Building structures is straight forward and easy to get used to
-Combat is what you expect from a game like this and is also easy to get used to
-Great voice acting, the Insectoid Advisor reminds of Waspinator from Beast Wars. Which is awesome.
Negatives:
-No options! What's up with that? I get that it's early access, but I'm disspointed I could not adjust the graphic quality or volume settings as well as the other options
-The difficulty ramps up increadibly quickly, too quickly. The first 3 stages were a peice of cake, but in stage 4 enemies literally swarm you before you have a chance to build up your defenses. I assume with the inclusion of the DNA resource, and the upgrade that come with it, stage 4 would be a lot more reasonable, but as of right now its too hectic and almost unplayable.
-No naming system. I want to name all my insectoid minions and build a connection with them as they level up.
With all that being said I would highly recommend The Hive and I look forward to updates that will make this game better.

Definitely a must play for tactical turn based fans.
At times it can be kind of clunky, and a little rough around the edges, but the game play is truly excellent, and in some areas superior to even XCOM.
The setting is a distinctly compelling mix of Fading Suns, Battletech, BSG, 40K, and its own ideas. If you love unleashing the fanatical wrath of space marines then you're in for a treat. Only these Templar are larger than Terminators. They drive Heavy Gear sized warmachines that overheat and dwarf normal sized humans. One of the games strengths is how it plays with this size disparity. You start out battling giant aliens that are equal to you in size. So once you start fighting actual humans, they seem so utterly puny and fragile, you truly feel like an unstoppable juggernaut. Just be careful because some of those humans have access to rocket launchers...
Missions offer a lot of variety, creativity, and clever design. Having played countless turn based tactical games, Templar Battleforce definitely sets a new standard in level design excellence. I'm tempted to list out all the epic and entertaining things to be encountered, but I don't want to spoil the thrill of discovering it for yourself. Let's just say, when I play a mission for the first time, I try to be prepared for everything, because it seems like just about anything could happen.
Fun tactical concepts like area-based-overwatch, scanners, melee vs range, fog-of-war, heat sinks, turrets, stealth, overheating, ordance, and so much more, all help the 8 different classes feel unique. Even within a class you are offered a lot of meaningful customize between talents, attributes, and equipment.
I held off buying this for a long time, but I'm so glad I took a chance on this one. It truly is a diamond in the rough and deserves all the praise.

'Soccertron' is obviously a creative developement of that idea - several 'sports' added along with modern physics engine and neon graphics. Если помните времена ДОС, то, вероятно, вспомните игру "Волейбол для автоматов" (1987), которая была весьма популярна в качестве случайного убийцы времени. "Соккертрон" однозначно является творческим развитием той идеи - добавлены новые "виды спорта", а также современная физика и неоновая графика. Боты хитры и настырны, сложные ситуации возникают каждую секунду, и после того, как привыкнешь к движениям героя (гораздо более навороченным, чем у предшественника) и управлению, эмоции текут рекой!

Templar Battleforce takes a crack at establishing a Warhammer 40k/Space Hulk-esque background lore with mediocre to debatable results, mostly conveying a knock-off feeling, with some moderately immersive element here and there, the vast tech tree being quite interesting.
Leveling up and introduction to stats could have been included in the tutorial or treated more extensively, to create an easier access and first steps to the game's system.
The gameplay itself is decent but the pixelated style ultimately fails to achieve any unique aesthetical charm other than "looks decades old", with extremely simple animations and sound effects.
Only at higher difficulties do soldiers die permanently, which is a feature I would have liked to be able to determine myself. Permadeath should not automatically equal stat-difficulty, as this reduces the options of creating a challenge on people's own terms.
- Vast technology tree
- Interesting variety in equipment with a certain Warhammer 40k/Space Hulk feel
- Outdated and charmless visuals
- Superficial tutorial
- Unbalanced difficulty options
- Helps itself rather shamelessly to Space Hulk/Warhammer 40k concepts. Then again GW might deserve it.
Overall I could have skipped on this.

A very cute game, somewhat reminiscant of Legend of Zelda, the way you traverse the land and find different upgrades across your adventures and find your self coming back to already examined areas to grab stuff you missed before now with the necessary abilities. Not incredibly difficult, played through it on the hardcore setting where things will frequently one shot you, but I never felt that I wasn't making progress because of that, once you learn the combos and stun capabilities as well as timing parries correctly, you become quite diffult to kill. The combat itself is very seemless, blending in your magic abilities with sword play very well, never felt a disconnect between the two, and some the monsters throughout the game, including bosses will require you to mix the two to defeat them while maintaining a decent combo, or rather beating them in a fluid manner. And the artwork in the game is very pretty, the motions everything makes in the game from the landscape to the actual character are very fluid, my only criticism is that towards the ending of the game you have two cutscenes that aren't in the actual game art style, rather a rather cheesy animation that tries to instill dramatic effect, but it can very distracting when you've played through the game for nearly 6 hours with the same art style and then suddenly it changes up on you.
All in all though, I recommend this game to anyone looking for a pick em up action-RPG that looks great, plays great, and is not that harsh on the wallet.

Not that this game seems to be in any desperate need of more positive reviews, but I had to put in my two cents. To tell a long story short, I think that Hotline Miami is a masterpiece of modern gaming.
The Pros:
Fantastic gameplay: Deaths are seemless into restarts as so not to be frustrating, the level design is fantastic, and the boss battles are memorable. Using every weapon feels great.
Crazy replayability: The main story isn't all that long, depending on how much you die, but there's a lot to do afterwards. The true ending requires going back to find all the secrets. If you want to 100% it like me, you have to get an A+ on every chapter, which is really hard, but so satisfying
Variability: Keeps the game fresh nicely. There are tons of weapons and guns, and over a dozen masks that can drastically change gameplay (or just add a filter, but still...)
Music: Has my second favorite soundtrack of all time- only second to Hotline Miami 2. The energetic, pounding house music fits perfectly with the gameplay and atmosphere.
Story: Hard to understand, but if you work for it, the story is really incredible. Most of the story is told through the enviroment, so you're left guessing on a lot of important information. The ambiguity is purpousful, and makes any glimmer of information you can find seem huge. HLM1 tells the how of the story, while HLM2 tells the why, but I think the combination of gameplay, sparse dialogue, and conflicting themes makes a much better story in HLM1.
Cons:
Uhhh? Sometimes the game doesn't register my finishers, which is annoying, but I can work with. The game crashes a little too often for my liking as well, but I can live with it.
All in all, I think this is an incredibly layered game. The gameplay, visuals, and sound are all great, but digging a little bit deeper can give you so much more. Many reviews would make HLM1 seem like a pointless slaughterfest, but there's a lot more than first meets the eye. I never thought I could become so attached to characters who hardly have any dialogue, if any at all. I might even go so far as to say the game has artistic qualities in how it uses ambiguity, enviroment, and gameplay to tell a compelling story. No steam library is complete without it.

This game is an online game where two players send balloons to try and push through the other's defense. This is definitely not a pay to win game, which is something rarely seen in a free to play game. This game has nice graphics that are not realistic and more on the cartoony side.
-===-
If you want an explanation of the game:
This game requires a lot of strategy. You select three towers to bring in a match. Towers will defend balloons, and you earn a certain amount of money every six seconds. The amount of money earned every six seconds starts at $250. This increases as you send balloons, but higher level balloons (such as MOABs) will decrease your amount of money gained. Balloons cost money to send, and towers cost money to build. If a certain number of balloons get through your defense, you lose the game. Each tower can be upgraded to buff it up. New towers are gained by playing more and buying them with the in game currency, medallions. Each match can take a long time to finish, but overall the game is fantastic.
-===-

Having played over 50 hours of Mafia 3 and having just finished the story I cannot understand all the hate.
This was probably the game that I enjoyed the most this year, I've seen persons calling it average and I'm left wondering how's that possible...
The scenario of the game is amazing, the city was very well designed, having more interiors than I ever found in any other similar game. The graphics do look good on the overall, being at times a key factor to add to the scenery. Although it must be said that they look good mostly due to effects and not to the textures them selves.
The sound track is probably the best that I ever seen in any game, simply amazing, adds a lot to the experience, the same can be said of the driving, phenomenal, probably the one that I've enjoyed the most, probably only coming behind the driver series, and even then I'm not sure if even that one is better.
Performance wise I can understand some the the critics, having a GTX 960 4GB I soon realised that I wouldn't be able to reach 60 fps on high settings. I accepted that and limited it to 30 fps, I must say that I didn't even feel the difference, the game ran very smoothly after the limitation. And if I personally don't think that 30 or 60 fps is that much of a diffence as long as the experience is smooth I do respect the opinion of those who think otherwise, the game should have indeed been better optimised.
Bug wise I didn't have many problems, I found some but not those much considering the time that I spent playing, to be honest the only one I can remember even made me laught so I can't complain.
The way in which the story was told was very well though, they made the narration look like a documentary of Lincoln Clay's life revealing more as you progress, the cut scenes and the voice act are spectacular, I must say that I missed a game that told a story so well for a long time.
The developers also paid attention to many small details, one of which that I found very interesting was the fact that the radio sound would get a disturbance while you drive in a long tunnel, very nice touch that adds to the immersion. But if they added stuff that I wasn't really expecting I must also say that they also missed important stuff, something that I found very intriguing was the fact of how the city has so much rail and yet I don't remember to see a single train or tram on the move.
The game start was very enjoyable, I liked the way in which they present the story but it is after 1-2hours into it that you start to realise the what you were presented at the start of the game won't be found im most of what comes next.
The story takes you on a personal vendetta but they made it too repetitive. They divided the map by districts, which one of them controlled by certain persons but this is where the problem starts, the way in which you take control of the districts are, meet with two persons of interest in that area that will each one give you info on a activity going on there, for example some districts have drug and prostitution rackets, each of these would be controled by a differente guy. After talking with your contact you go on to sabotage these rackets, you do this by going around the city getting info, killing guys and destroying supplies, eventually after taking down both rackets you'll draw the the lieutenant of that district out and then go after him, after you kill him the district is yours. Eventually about every two lieutenants you'll also take down a capo.
The problem here is that the map has 12 districts and that process will be the same for all of them, even the animations are the same, not to mention how some places are reused, going back to a place that I already cleared out to find full of enemies and have to clear it out again doesn't make much sense to me. This is where the developers failed badly.
Everything looks amazing, even the story is good and told in an amazing way but the missions come no where close to it.
Usually the missions connected to  lieutenants and capos felt more interesting but even then not much different from the rest, go somwhere and kill a lot of guys, that's basically what you'll be doing the whole game.
And considering that you'd expect the AI to be a bit smarter, I enjoyed the shootings but the enemies were really dumb at times, making the game feel somewhat easy even on hard difficulty.
Something else that I didn't understand is why they removed stuff such as cloth shops, gun shops, fuel stations, etc and didn't have car customization at launch. To be honest the game feels rushed, they should have had more time to complete the game.
Overall I had a great time playing the game and consider it well above averenge giving it a 7/10. But that leaves me very disapointed because if the mission system had been better designed this would easily be a 9/10. The game is good but had potential to be a LOT better.

If you ignore all of the abysmal missions and forestry garbage and focus on what the game does well - the offroad simulator - you'll feel that you got something of value.
The forestry game element is puzzling, frustrating and frankly feels like it was tacked on: pick up logs with a crane, put them on a trailer and then swear and curse when the trailer won't accept the logs because it isn't perfectly straight-on and level to the truck it's affixed to. If you give up and drive off with the logs simply placed in the trailer but not technically loaded, you aren't allowed to unload them at the destination. For those unfamiliar (i.e. reading this review), I'm not sure that there's a flat surface in the entire game, and certainly not one where you can collect lumber.
The multiplayer is good fun, though the lack of content other than the odious forestry minigame limits the playability and it isn't long before people decide that getting bogged in one virtual mud pit is very much like any other and go back to other games with actual content. Leaving you with a most unsatisfactory single player experience.
The camera movements are somewhat limited, and there are a lot of times that you really wish that you had that little bit more freedom to see what you were doing, especially when genuinely off-roading in the UAZ.
Finally, the wheel controls are a bit odd: I couldn't map the d-pad on my Logitech wheel (the game treats them like mouse movements), and the analog buttons wouldn't work as ranges only as on/off triggers.
Pros: Entertaining off-road simulator made better, albiet temporarily, with friends.
Cons: Atrocious forestry minigame. Lack of content.
Until additional content is released and the utterly absurd loading mechanic overhauled, not recommended.

Warmode is a poorly made multiplayer Russian FPS that has a sort of "it's so bad, its good quality". Maps are relatively small, and there are only a few. The graphics are equivalent to a bad looking PS2 game. Bodies ragdoll limply and sometimes enemy players will die in their normal standing animation in air if they were killed while in air on standing on props.
